Damn! I just put a huge gash in my hand while cutting vegetables for cooking class. I immediately put a paper towel around my hand to cover the blood; I hate the site of blood and my own will infidelity make me pass out. I raise my other hand to tell the teacher I need to go to the nurse, and she allows me since this isn't the first time a student cut themselves in her class. While on the way to the nurse, I look at the paper towel to see if I'm going to need stitches, but there isn't any red on the paper towel. "That's weird." I say out loud I pull off the towel to see the cut and there is no blood, no bone or muscle, instead I am looking at wires. I scream at the shock. It's like in star wars when Luke lost his hand to Darth Vader except I'm not a jedi, I'm human; at least I think I am. I run home hoping my mom is home to tell me what is going on. When I get there both my Mom and Dad are home and I burst through the door panting. "Honey what's wrong?" My Mom asked concerned I hold up my exposed wiring, "This, this is what's wrong with me!" My Mom looked as shocked as I was when I saw, but my Dad just sat with a disappointed look "I was hoping you wouldn't find out about this, I was hoping I could keep it a secret from both of you." "Honey, what are you talking about? What is our son?" My Mom asked worried "Well," he started "it happened after you gave birth to our son, the real one. He died of complications, you were asleep when the doctors told me, but they offered me some new program they wanted to prototype. A robotic child that will grow up like normal, but will never get sick, never have long term issues but grow to be old like any other human." "So that's what I am, a prototype?" I asked tearing up. How could I be tearing if I am a robot? Or be as angry as I am, this doesn't make sense "The doctors were working with the FBI to see if they can create a robot with such realistic artificial intelligence that they could use them for espionage. When you were growing up, you learned to feel like a human would and you learned how to behave like a human would." "I can't believe this." My Mom said, crying now. "One however, the government wanted to take you to a facility to test the results of you, but I always deny them the access to you." My Dad said confidently. "You may be a robot, but you're still my son and I couldn't love you anymore than I already do." Now I really can't control my tears, I run to my Dad to hug him when he pulls some sort of taser out of his pocket, I hit the floor and unable to move. "I can't believe he found out." My Dad said with an annoyed tone to his voice. "What are we going to do?" My Mom asked hovering over me. "We can wipe the memory for today, it's not the first time this happened." I want to fight back but I can't, all I see is darkness taking over my vision. The alarm clock goes off and I put it to snooze. "Phillip! Wake up you got ta get up for class!" Dad yells from the kitchen "Coming Dad!" I answer I really don't want to go today, I get nervous around knives for some reason.

Roger checks his revolver again. It's still loaded. His heart pounds harder than it ever has before. He wants to wait for backup, but he might escape. He couldn't let this monster escape one more time. He holds the revolver in his hands and kicks in the door. He rushes in and sees something that he never expected: his wife. "Josie? What are you doing here?" She isn't tied up. She's fully dressed, no bruises or marks of any kind. "Hi Roger, I'm sorry it's come to this." "Come to what? Where is he?" She stands and walks over to him. She kisses him and grabs his gun. Josie unloads it and throws it into a corner. "I don't understand. You've been working with him this entire time? Our marriage was a lie?" "No," her eyes well up with tears, "it wasn't a lie. Our marriage was real and my love for you is genuine. It just wasn't meant to be." "What is going on?" "You were never chasing a he. You were chasing me." Roger laughs. It's the most ridiculous thing he's ever heard. "C'mon, Josie, that's insane." He reaches out to her, but she pulls away. "Has he hurt you? Drugged you? He didn't..... force himself on you, did he?" "I am Joe Commons. I was able to stay ahead of you all this time because I am, er, maybe was your wife. I stayed ahead of you by deceiving you, but that wasn't my intention. I love you very much." "You killed my partner. No, he killed my partner. That madman killed my partner and 16 other people. Now, you're telling me you're actually him. That can't be." "I couldn't sabotage you. You'd figure it out, so I gave up." "No, there's a mole in the department." "There isn't. There never was." She says, angry. "I don't believe you. I can't. This is a lie." "I can provide information only the killer would know." "No, he told you." "Fine, he told me. I had a different plan, but you won't accept it. In that closet, you will find an unconscious man. He did these crimes. The last three should be easy to prove. The rest will be charged to or at least attributed to him." Roger opens the closet door to find a man tied and gagged. He turns back to look at his wife who now looks away from him. The man is unconscious. Roger picks up his gun and loads a round into it. He turns towards his wife and aims his revolver at her. Then, he turns and shoots the man in the closet. The story would be easy now. His nemesis kidnapped his wife and was waiting in the closet for him. He flew out, instinct took over. He shot him. End of story.

"I enjoyed our last date. I have something for you and we need to meet again." Pushy hey. Sarah was pretty shy last time I met her but hell, at least someone's taking the lead this time. Jimmy thought as he reread the message ten minutes early by the fountain. By the gate at the end of the path she walked into sight and seemed to stand about 1000ft tall and full of poise. Such life filled every breath as she walked with shining eyes and composed grace. Jimmy became acutely aware that his jaw was hanging open. As this glittering effigy of Jimmy's vague recollection approached he stood slowly. Almost bending on one knee before gathering the strength to stand. He was in a defiant mood. That's the secret power of odd socks he thought. "Jimmy. You're looking handsome I must say. Thanks for meeting me." "Sarah, your looking...... Sprightly." "Elaborate Jimmy. I've no time for you mincing words." Jimmy had no protection. The words hit him like a delicate song delivered like a jackhammer. They commanded obedience. "Its like you've been supercharged. Like you could control the stars with a wave of your hand. I'm an open book to you. The Sarah I knew is still there, but her soul is different. Its grown and is spilling out of you." He fell silent and looked down. "Jimmy. I've used you as an objective benchmark. I needed to know who I am now I've seen so much and lost so many. I brought this for you." As sarah held out a beautiful flower unlike Jimmy had ever seen. He didn't care about plants but this was special. "We're not going to see each other again. In another life I would have loved you. Goodbye." As Jimmy looked up from the flower in his hand she had disappeared. Yet all around kids and adults didn't notice a thing. Was it not for the flower it would have been a dream. He suddenly felt the urge to never wear odd socks again.

Everyone has a voice inside their head. Usually the voice is there to bring up embarrassing things you did in high school and remind you of important deadlines after they've passed. Jared had two voices in his head. No more, no less. One voice was his own, but the other voice was different. For starters, it wasn't his own voice. It was the voice of a middle aged British man. This is somewhat peculiar since Jared was a twenty-five year old from Connecticut who had never been abroad. Jared never bothered to discuss this with anyone. He just accepted it as the norm since it had been with him for as long as he could remember. To make matters worse, the voice's sole function in his head was to narrate his life. Jared couldn't converse with this voice no matter how much he tried. It simply narrated his actions and feelings. Much to Jared's frustration, it was often wrong about what it was saying. There was always a modicum of truth to what it said, but it twisted the truth in bizarre ways. It used to drive him crazy. Nowadays, he had mostly learned to ignore it. Having a British man in your head narrating your life makes it difficult to socialize at times. Jared realized he couldn't trust the voice early on, when he was in elementary school. He was eating lunch with one of the few friends he had when the voice claimed that his friend had stolen some grapes out of his lunch bag. After accusations declared and a friendship soured, Jared found out that the voice had fingered the wrong kid. Someone else had stolen his grapes. Jared blamed his lack of social skills on the British voice. He was shy around most people, and seeing any halfway attractive female left his palms sweaty and his mind blank. Tired of the relentless loneliness and lack of intimacy, Jared tried his hand at online dating. He enjoyed using Tinder. It allowed him time to craft thoughtful responses and to hide from the inevitable gauntlet of face to face interaction. Eventually, he matched with a girl named Vanessa. For some reason she decided that Jared tickled her fancy and agreed to meet up for a date. The plan was to meet at a nearby cafe one evening. When the night came, Jared was a nervous wreck. He showered and was in the process of shaving when the voice chimed in. Jared had waited for this night all his life. He couldn't contain his bloodlust any longer. " Ow! " Jared shrieked. He cut himself with his razor at that last line. Bloodlust? What narrative was the voice spinning tonight? He finished shaving, and started dressing himself He chose dark clothing, for stealth. He donned his favorite leather boots in case he needed to take her into the woods. " What the hell are you talking about? " Jared demanded with incredulity. This voice was making him sound like a serial killer. He did not need this on his first date. " Whatever, fuck it " he said, to his empty room. Jared had been stalking Vanessa's social media profiles for weeks. He pored over every detail he could learn about her. He was obsessed with her. He loved her. He wanted her dead. Jared seriously considered cancelling the date as he walked towards the cafe. This voice was pissing him off, and he didn't want to make a bad first impression. He continued on. He had already cancelled twice because of nerves, and he knew he couldn't again. Jared walked at a slow and deliberate pace. As each boot step squashes the grass beneath him, he imagines himself crushing Vanessa's windpipe under his foot. " No I don't " he growled to himself through clenched teeth as he fought to keep the proposed image out of his head. He walked up to the cafe and saw Vanessa through the window. She looked even better than he had imagined. He wanted to take her behind the cafe and choke the life out of her immediately. Jared made a mental note to see a psychiatrist the next day. The date went better than he expected despite the horror story unfolding in his head. Vanessa was incredibly easy to talk to, and she seemed not to notice, or at least ignore his preoccupation. Every second passed with agony, Jared just wanted to get her out of the cafe so he could make her heart stop beating. After the fifth grisly murder scenario proposed by the narrator, Jared had to excuse himself to the bathroom. He splashed water on his face and stared at himself in the mirror. " Stop what you're doing! " He ordered the voice with ferocity. A man using the urinal quickly finished peeing and scurried out of the bathroom. The anger was building in Jared. He knew it was time for someone to die. He could see it. Blood everywhere. He longed for it. It was inevitable. It always had been. Jared stopped talking to himself in the bathroom, so as not to appear completely insane, and returned to his date. " Are you okay? " Vanessa asked, " You seem upset. " " I'm fine, I just have a lot on my mind from work " he lied. " How about we go back to my place then? I'll make you a drink " she said. Jared couldn't believe she was inviting him back. He thought for sure that she wasn't into him. " Sure, I'm down with that " Jared started to feel more at ease. They exited the cafe and began walking to Vanessa's which was only a few minutes away. Soon. Soon, Jared would be alone with her. He walked with purpose to her apartment. The end is nigh. " I usually don't take people back to my place this soon. I just feel like I know you since we've been talking on Tinder for so long. You're not going to murder me are you? " Vanessa asked playfully. Yes, without a doubt " No! I promise " he said, feeling somewhat uneasy. They entered Vanessa's apartment. She poured him a drink, and after they clinked glasses, she excused herself to the kitchen. The time is now. Jared knew death was approaching. Jared simply rolled his eyes, he wasn't going to let this old Brit ruin his evening. Vanessa came back into the room. He turned around as she plunged a butcher's knife into his stomach. He looked up at Vanessa in shock. Her face lit up with delight and she let out a sickly cackle. Jared, still in shock, shoved Vanessa to the ground and pulled the knife out of his stomach. He ran out of her apartment doubled over, clutching his wound. He made it to the stairwell when she caught up with him. She swung at him wildly with another, more serrated knife. Thanks to the adrenaline pumping through his veins, he felt nothing as she cut into his forearm. The knife became lodged in his arm; Jared saw his opening. He grabbed Vanessa and, with all the strength he could muster, threw her down the stairs. Vanessa tumbled down the stairs and landed on her head with a satisfying crack against the cement. Blood oozed out of her skull, but she was still moving. Jared hobbled down the stairs. He felt alive. He looked at her in disgust and crushed her windpipe with his boot. The first kill is always messy.

Lucifer had spent his life trying to avoid the shadow of God, which was really quite a pain in the ass. The old man really was a conniving, controlling, dogmatic little bastard, and he seemed to be everywhere, what with the omnipresence and whatnot. To get away from him, Lucifer had been forced to take less than desirable real estate, but Hell wasn't all that bad. Hot, smelly, and crowded, but really, there were worse conditions in your average subway station. Lucifer had made a good life in Hell, all in all. Best of all, God seemed to ignore him other than instructing his prophets to write cutting rumors about him in that big fancy burn book of his. At least, that whole teenage-girl-style passive aggression seemed to be the case until God sent that hot shot Jesus with all that godly divinity down to clean up the joint. Lucifer didn't know how God had managed to create an ass that was more self-righteous than he was, but somehow that old fart had done it, and in strode in Jesus like he was the freaking savior of the world. Jesus did not belong in Hell. Hell was dirty, filthy, and well, hellish. Yet Jesus was wearing white robes and sandals. Didn't he know he could get some sort of weird toe fungus walking around like that? Lucifer guessed one sweep of God's magic wand would probably take care of it, but still; it hardly seemed hygienic. Nonetheless, Jesus the celestial and impractical had reached one hand out of his pristine white robes, and he smote the hell out of Lucifer. Or the Lucifer out of Hell, as it would be. Lucifer hadn't even really known that he could die. Cast out of heaven, yeah, but die? That was a new one. What was stranger was waking up, not in fluffy clouds or in sulfur pools, but in a vast meadow that never ended beneath a sky that never clouded, where time was nonexistent. Lucifer could feel the pulse of each soul, and in turn, his soul was felt by all. Gone was heaven and Hell. Gone was judgment. Gone was God. What was left was paradise. Lucifer stood up, ready to embrace this new eternity, until he himself was embraced, much, much too tightly. " My dearest brother, I offer my most sincere condolences. I should have seen that it was not my place to try to force you to the path of righteousness. " Jesus said, as sanctimonious as ever. " From now on, brother, we shall never be parted! " Lucifer supposed the smiting must have been reflected or backfired or something, and somehow this Jesus prick died too and had joined him in this afterlife. Oh hell, now Lucifer was going to have to find some forsaken corner of land in whatever this place was to find a way to avoid this pious prick. " Goddammit! " Lucifer swore. Sometimes a guy can't catch a break.

I was tired. I was returning home from a business trip in Chicago, and all I wanted was to get home. What I did not want was to talk to other people. I was minding my own business, sitting in the aisle seat, while the lady sitting to my right decided it would be a great idea to chat my ear off. The wrinkles around her lips danced when she spoke, and her breath smelled like coffee. Her hair was a bit too red for her age, and lipstick stained her teeth. "I'm really quite excited to see my grandson," she babbled, "He's graduating law school." I inhaled sharply. I just needed to make it to Newark, and I would be fine. I could do this. "He's also recently engaged!" she exclaimed, throwing her hands in the air. "Did I mention that?" Yes, yes you did. "He's got a great girl," she smiled, her lipstick stained tooth showing. "She's smart, beautiful, and she's studying to be a pharmacist." That's great. "She's going to prescribe drugs! How exciting is that!" Very. Suddenly, a man with dark sunglasses and a baseball hat casually strutted down the aisle, looking for his seat. Please sit in between me and this lady with nothing better to do than to annoy me. Please. As he reached our row, he brushed past me, sliding into the middle seat. He didn't look too friendly, so I was happy I had the opportunity for peace and quiet. I must have dozed off right after takeoff, because I awoke to the man staring at me, smiling. He had taken off his sunglasses, and I could see the red in his eyes. "It really is a shame," he whispered. I sat up in my seat, straightening out my jacket sleeves. "Pardon?" I mumbled, my voice still groggy. "This plane isn't going to make it to Newark," he exhaled, turning back. I froze. Who was this man, and what was he talking about? He put his sunglasses on, leaning his head back against the headrest. "Sir?" I exclaimed, my heart racing. No response. "Sir!" I yelled once more, this time more forcefully. Still no answer. I placed my arm on his shoulder and shook him. I needed to tell someone about this, soon. I unbuckled my seatbelt, and just as I was standing up, I felt a cold, clammy hand around my forearm. I turned around, slowly, to see the strange man breathing down my neck. "It's no use," he grinned, "time has run out," he laughed, slowly sinking back into his seat. Before I could even think of what to do, the pilot came over the intercom, and the plane hit turbulence. "We're experiencing some engine difficulties at the moment," he paused, "but we ask that you stay calm." People around me began to look around, and worried voices filled the cabin. "We urge that you follow the emergency protocols, and stay seated." The red-haired woman turned towards me, her eyes filled with fear. "I'm not going to see my grandson, am I?" she muttered quietly, her voice one of many in the sea of screams. The man next to me continued to sit relaxed, still laughing. The plane took a sudden dive, and the oxygen masks released. The screams increased, as all of us now knew what was coming. The strange man was right. We never did make it to Newark. My last memories were a grandmother gushing about her grandson and a strange man telling me my fate. It really was a shame.

The gavel fell, and recess began. One by one, the jury filed out into the corridor. A tall figure in white motioned them on to the jury room. "Let me know if you need anything." The figure intoned from one of its three faces. "And remember, you must all come to a unanimous decision." The twelve jurors shuffled into the room and took their seats. "This never gets any more interesting." sighed an elderly gentleman as he pulled out a chair for the slightly younger looking woman next to him. "Think how I feel, having to do this twice." the woman smiled. There was a cough from the other side of the room. Nobody had I told i the jurors to assemble themselves based on their feelings for the accused, but naturally, they had arranged themselves this way. "If this trial is anything like the last one, I suppose you're wonderin' why I hate your son." Juror 4 was a woman, about 60 years old, her skin yellow and taut. Jurors 1 and 3 pursed their lips together. Juror 5 got to his feet. "Now, now," said the man with the slicked back hair. "I had the pleasure of knowing Wi - the defendant - only a few short years, and yet in that time I knew him as the most charming young man I ever did meet. Hate is a strong word Juror 2, a child of about 8 years old, stuck out her tongue and made a loud raspberry noise. "You don't know anything!" she said, and folded her arms petulantly, "I hate William." An air of awkwardness descended on the room. Most of the jurors remembered Sally Adams. She'd been a bit of a bully, back before the sickness, but everyone knew how big a crush she'd had on William Waters - and everyone remembered how just two months before she went into hospital, he'd refused to take her to the dance'in case she falls over again and pees herself.' Surprisingly, it was Juror 4 who spoke up again. "Now I'm not saying that William wasn't a little shit to teach. I'm not saying he wasn't spoilt and childish. But Sally, you and he were kids. He didn't know any better." Juror 7, a young man in a letterman jacket with a bandage covering the hideous gash on his forehead, followed up. "He cried at your memorial. Nearly dropped his candle." Juror 9 barked in agreement. "Does anyone here," began the slick-haired uncle, "have any grievance against the defendant which they genuinely believe, beyond all doubt, that he does not feel deeply apologetic about?" The room erupted into whispers, and heckling. It seemed that for all their posturing and heckling on the stand, not one of the jurors could say for sure that they genuinely hated the defendant. Certainly, they didn't hate him enough to condemn him to hell. It seemed as though a unanimous decision had been reached - and they hadn't even needed a coffee break. But then the shadow in the back of the room raised their hand. Juror 12 had declined to take a seat with the others, instead opting to go and stand by the window, just looking out at the sky. For the most part, the other jurors were very comfortable about this. For one thing, none of them knew Juror 12. They could not place their features from elementary or highschool, college, or workplace. Throughout the trial, 12 had remained quiet, never taking their eyes from the figure of the defendant. "I'm sorry." Juror 12 croaked. "But I feel as though I do hate the defendant. Enough to send him to hell." Their voice was cracked, as though they were speaking through several layers of grit. As one, the room glanced towards them and immediately averted their eyes. Juror 12 was not a nice sight to see. They wore no clothes - not that it mattered, since they were barely even recognisable as human. Their skin, the texture and colour of a boiled lobster, folded around their neck and armpits like congealed fat in a pan, the ripples broken at points with jagged scar tissue. They had no genitalia, only a hideous pile of bubbling flesh, and their chest was a lattice of criss-crossing scars. Their face was the worst thing to behold - one eye dangled limply from its socket while the other bulged out like a balloon, horrible and red. There were no teeth in their mouth, only bloody gums, and their hair was patchy, as though it had been shaved by a mad barber. The assembled jurors looked at one another. Trembling, Juror 3 stood to speak. "Who are you? How do you know my son?" A tear dribbled from the corner of Juror 12's one intact eye. "I was his victim."

Grasping the freshly charged, slightly battered old phone protectively in one hand, she sat by her living room table and straightened the photo of her family. Her sister should be calling any minute now. There it is. "Hey, sis." "Hey..." "How's your trip?" "There was an accident on the highway. The car's in pieces, mum and dad are hurt pretty bad. I haven't seen them move in a while." She lit the candle beside the photo, and took a deep breath before responding. "Are you alright?" " ..... my head. Oh, I'm feeling a little dizzy. And it's cold." A tear came to her eye. This moment always tugged on her heart. "I already called emergency. Gave them my GPS. Did I already say that? I feel like I've told you all this before." The voice was trailing off, like it always does. "Keep talking to me. Did you have fun with them? Do you think you got the job?" "Yeah, everything went great. Aside from right now, it was the best week of my life." "Well, I'm glad," she whispered, forcing the words out. "I've missed you. So much." She wiped away more tears. The calls were frightening and confusing at first, but she eventually learned to take small comfort in them. "I can hear the sirens now. They'll be here soon. I'm so tired." "It's ok. You can go to sleep. I love you." And just like that, the phone shut down. Low battery. It will be another year before it will hold a charge.

Slight variation of the prompt, still fits I think? First time writing in here so not sure He looks down. From up here, it suddenly looks a lot higher as he thought it would. The cold rain dripping down his neck keeps him awake, even though that's exactly what he wants to escape. While the rain slowly mixes in with the salt of his tears, he takes a deep breath. The muffled sound of sirens in the distance reminds him that this is the right choice. It's the only choice. And then all the sounds just seem to stop. No more bombs going off, no more sirens, just the wind rushing past him as he realises the pavement is getting closer and closer. The years rush past him as he falls, his childhood, university, marriage, and then that dreadful day. That dreadful day the end of the world started, without anyone even really knowing. As he keeps falling, out of nowhere a door appears in his mind. It immediately opens and brings him back to the first dreadful day. Many dreadful days had followed from there on. He sees himself, he knows what he did. He chose a leader for his nation. Still falling through his memory, the ink suddenly shifts place. And with that, the future to believe in became history. More doors open, but all he can see is that ink shifting. He chose for this to happen, just as he now chose for this to end. The final door makes place for the pavement he expected to reach so much faster. The pavement he expected to reach before he knew.

Nathan rapped his knuckles on the huge, green shoulder plates next to him "Have you seen Peach? Someone's at the door" A gruff, half robotic voice answered "She popped next door to Lara's. We ran out of ice." Nathan nodded and turned to open the door. "Hey, welcome to..... oh, Sorry. I thought you were here for the thing. Peach is at another castle, but she'll be right back. But I can show you to the bathroom if you want to get started? I didn't know anything was wrong, but I saw Donkey Kong in there earlier, so I can put two and two together" A big mustache and its accompanying red hat were greatly obscuring two small eyes staring up at Nathan in mute silence. "Oh, right, sorry. Uh, I don't know Spanish, and Ancient Mayan doesn't have a word for bathroom. So..... This way" Nathan gestured broadly for the small plumber to follow him and tried to move through the crowd. A tall woman in a black skinsuit slid through the crowd and stopped in front of them. "Nathan, Who's your friend?" "This is the plum - " "IT'S A ME! MAAARIO!" The man shouted The sudden eruption of noise shocked Nathan a bit. "This is Mario. He's here to fix the plumbing." "Ohhh, yes. Donkey Kong was in there earlier." She turned and leaned down to face Mario "I'm Bayonetta. Nice to meet you." The visible portions of the man's cheeks turned, literally, as red as his hat and he resumed his characteristic silence as she walked away. Mario and Nathan continued. "Hey, I'm sorry about earlier. You weren't saying anything, so I just assumed..... It's not'cause you're a plumber or anything..... Hey, look at that: here we are!" He pushed the door open and gestured inside "I'll just leave you to it." Nathan walked away quickly, leaving Mario confused outside the bathroom. He turned to face the rest of the party, happy to await Peach. A kid of indeterminate age wearing a green tunic and hat approached him and nodded. Mario seemed happy to see him and nodded back before shrugging with his palms out. The Green hat tipped toward the kitchen where Mario saw a pointed-eared princess. Mario raised his eyebrows inquisitively. The green tunic shrugged and wore a contented smile. Mario smiled back and gave a small bow at the good news. The two friends continued to catch up as Mario waited for his Princess.

Monroe and I looked at the body. It was an odd way to die, a crazy contraption consisting of a gun, a clamp, and various mechanisms and electronics that had presumably pulled the trigger. It seemed like a very complicated way to kill yourself. On the positive side, it was suicide which was still plenty of annoying paperwork, but considerably less trouble than a murder investigation. " Do you think it's true? ," I asked Munroe. " Seems like bullshit, but who knows? " I reread the note one more time: Quantum Immortality Experiment 160. By now, I am absolutely certain that the many worlds interpretation of quantum physics is true. Every day, I trigger the quantum random number generator with a 5050 chance, and thus far, every day I have survived. The odds of this event happening are 1 in 2159, which is essentially impossible. Unless all possible things happen, in which case I have died in many universes but this is the one where I lived. Until now. If you're reading this note, you're in a universe where I died on the 160th attempt. But don't worry. In another universe I'm still very much alive. Sorry for the body. I wondered if this was some sort of physics breakthrough that would shake quantum physics, or just a garden variety nutter. I considered what to do... I pushed the button on the quantum random number generator, and looked at the result. Heads: I called my sister, who taught engineering at a local community college. She was no science genius, but she knew people who knew people, and the news got passed along. As I understand it, it's a pretty big deal. Tails: I crumpled the note. Ah well, so much for that " many worlds interpretation ."

It was Silvia's and my 2nd anniversary dating together. Despite a really rocky start and some strange moments, things seemed to be going really well. Our interests, temperments, and even our crazy sides matched. We met at an anime convention. She was looking over the latest re-releases of Battle Princess Mintaka. I don't know why, but I felt compelled to strike up a conversation. Well, it was probably the fact she was a fiery red-haired, piercing green eyed, freckled, glasses wearing, anime-interested young woman with a figure that my baser instincts had only theorized could exist. I may have been a goofy, tall and bulky dork..... But..... I have a near encyclopedic knowledge of Battle Princess Mintaka on my side. Fate may have been throwing me a pity softball on this one, but damned if I wasn't going to swing for the fences on it. So..... Two years, a whole host of convention going, and a lot of learning experiences..... We were still together and I didn't see anything stopping us. She got her dissertation together and defended it. With the Ph. D. in hand and some noted papers published, the university couldn't wait for her to apply for some open positions they'd been dying to fill. I was able to pull a few strings to get into the IT department with the help of an old friend who managed to find himself there after a big career change. So..... The next big step I figured was seeing if she wanted to move in with me. I managed to get a ridiculous price on a foreclosure property, and I had been living there for some time. Silvia is practically here all the time and the rent for anything nicer than a single bedroom apartment around this town is ridiculous. So, 2nd anniversery, I figured..... Why not ask? We decided to keep it simple this anniversary. Giving some craziness that happened during the first one, that Silvia still doesn't feel comfortable talking about..... Simpler is better. A nice day trip to some parts of the state we hadn't seen before, lunch at some place we found on the web, going over to the theatre to see the new Deadpool movie (Her suggestion, I love this woman), and dinner at the usual nice place we go to went we need a little fancy dining to bring up our spirits. We are hanging out on the couch. She's curled up with a blanket in my arms. She looks happy and content. Seems like a successful anniversary so far. I was tempted to put off asking her about moving in. I really didn't want to give Murphy's Law a chance to throw everything for a loop. But, hell..... You got ta know sometime right? "Hey, Silvia?" "Yes?" "I was thinking..... You are over here a lot anyway, you need a place to stay in the future, and well..... We've been together for two years. If you are comfortable with it, I'd really like to see how we are together, living in the same place." Okay. Logical reasoning presented, reason for the question revealed, and option to gracefully back out allowed. Worst case probably, "No, let's give it some more time." Best case: "Hell yes!" The sudden slight shudder of Silvia snapping to full consciousness and the odd feeling of the room's energy changing was not in any of the predicted outcomes. Oh shit, I'd somehow hit a critical snag. Silvia slowly pushes herself up and sits upright on the couch. The blanket slips away and she just sits there in uncomfortable contemplation. This is not good. She's normally a very confident and expressive woman. Seeing her this subdued and nervous..... This was shades of the last anniversary right here. I'm not going to allow that to happen again. "Hey, there's no pressure or anything. I just figured it might be something to think about. I think everything is going great between you and me. I've got a place, you are looking for a place. And there's no one else who I could think of that'd make this place more of a home for the both of us. If it's too much to ask, just say so. And we'll think about it later and A meek and saddened voice creeps from Silvia, "I want to. sniff I really do. I just- I just- I just don't know if you'd accept me." Okay. I'm confused. "Accept you? Have I not accepted you before? I accept you as you are before me. There's nothing I can think of that "I'm a demon." "A what?" "Demon." "You get a bit difficult some times, but you're hardly a Silvia shoots up from the couch, turns around to me, and holds her arms to the sides with tears in her eyes, "sniff I'll show you. It's best for the both of us to make it quick." The facade fades away. Silvia's long red hair, turns a silvery white. Her skin goes from the freckled pale to a gray with darker gray markings. Two swept back horns anchored in the sides of her forehead appear. But as strange as what has changed is, she still has that same figure, that beautful face, and the piercing green eyes that are more radiant than ever. "You know me as Silvia Carter. I'm..... I'm..... I'm Silvianistria Nostromandeus of the 3rd Order of Orion..... Former servant and advisor to the Battlemistress and Queen of the 3rd Order of Orion Lady Oriana Nox." She looks at me, expecting a certain reaction. I gaze into those same eyes. She's scared. It actually all makes sense to me now. We got A LOT to talk about. And she's not the only one with a few secrets to tell, but first things first. I take her hands into mine and never breaking eye contact with hers. I crack that smirk that she hates to love, "If you are the same woman that was nearly late to her dissertation defense because of an argument with me about how there is no way that Battle Princess Mintaka could have used the Gauntlet of the Guardian to defeat Lord Izo..... Then you are the same woman I've loved and will always love." This isn't the reaction she expected. After a brief moment of confusion, I witness one of the few moments she's ever been delighted to be absolutely wrong. She gracefully collapses into an embrace around my neck, one of her horns glances me in forehead with a light thunk. That'll take some getting used to. We hold each other and eventually start airing out all our laundry. A few hours later...... "So, that's me. Once an undisputed master advisor, mage, and alchemist to one of the Queens to the Dark Realms. Then Queen Nox decided to listen to that idiot Wester and got her aass royally kicked and banished to realms that even the darkest mages dare not even chart. Out of work and trapped on Earth. Thankfully, certain organizations offered me a chance at a life here on this planet with giving them a bunch of insider info." "I always wondered how they got all that info in those Battle Princess Mintaka books." "Yah, I kind of got into them while trying to see how they portrayed all us on the Dark Realm side." "They were pretty kind with your portrayal." "They still cleaned up the rest of the group. Great gods, most of Queen Nox's crew were complete perverts. I was so glad that Lord Izo got absolutely annihilated by Mintaka. He ran back to the Dark Realms and I haven't heard a thing about him since." "Grr..... Fucker deserved it." "You really don't like that guy. Every time that name gets brought up you ALWAYS emit this aura of spite and ire, that I never sense from you any other time." Shit. Well..... she's got me. Let's get all the laundry hanging out. "There's a reason. And as a bonus, it'll prove you right." This has her attention now. I feel her leaning in and her eyes trying to decipher what I was going to say. "The Gauntlet of the Guardian didn't leave Lord Izo and jump to Mintaka." "Yes. Because the Gauntlet will only jump on its own to someone trying to defend who they love and care for in their time of greatest need." "Yes..... Ah..... Those scars on my body, those weren't from electrical arcs. They were I don't get a chance to complete my sentence before Silvia is reaching under my shirt and feeling the various scarring I got a long time ago. "Holy shit! These are magical blast burn scars! The residual magic is so weak I could never pick it up while maintaining my illusion and shape change spell. Now, I can sense it all..... By the gods! How did you live through this Silvia hands held my right arm. Her fingertips sweep around. She's finally sensing the residual magic of what was on there. "You wore the..... THE..... Gauntlet of the Guardian?!" "Yes." "The bystander that attempted to save Mintaka and friends in issue 126 where Mintaka finally confronts Lord Izo?" "Me." "The gauntlet went to?" "Me." "Because WHO were you defending?" "My little sister." " ............!!!" "Yes." I think it'll be a LONG while before I see that degree of shock, confusion, and bewilderment in Silvia's face. And I really hope I'm not the one to cause it next time. I see her bite her lower lip and flash a concerned look my way. "Do you still want me to come over to your family's place this Thanksgiving? That might be REALLY awkward..... and possibly dangerous." "Don't worry. My sister wasn't good with the sensory powers before, and she hasn't used them in at least ten years. We should be fine." "But, what about Horus her magical cat?!" "Don't worry. Horus and I go back. I've helped him out a number of times. He'll keep it quiet." Plus, the bastard owes me a big one after nearly getting caught by the magical equivalent of the FBI trying to move his stash of Star Hemp to a new safe place. We both lay on the couch, back to that comfortable and content point again. "So..... you okay with moving in?" "Ha. Yes. I'm actually looking forward to it now." "Cool. Got to admit, it was nice getting everything out there." "No kidding. Strange world we live in. I'm just glad I can finally drop the shape change spell around you." "Speaking of which, you wouldn't happen to have THAT uniform still?" All I am able to get from Silvia is that evil little grin.

'I, Sir Geoffrey was raised to be the best knight of our time, even as a child I was trained rigorously and without pause. Every day, I felt the handle of my sword with my bare skin, the heavy chain-mail weighing down my tired shoulders and my helmet obscuring my vie 'Is now really the time?' Asked Marp. 'I am explaining to you my backstory.' Argued Geoffrey. Sir Geoffrey was huddled up behind a rock while the other side was being ferociously incinerated by a dragon's flame. The heat was incredible, beyond any sensation he had felt before. If it were not for Marp's magic, he'd be toast under the heavy plate armor. Geoffrey was indeed a great knight, the best of the best. He had suffered trials after trials, never losing the ambition to become the most chivalrous, famous and courageous knight in all of history. In exchange, he had sacrificed his personal life, love life and all other hobbies. Had you asked Geoffrey to quilt, he'd try his best and fail miserably. If you had called quilting a "trial" in becoming a great knight, he'd learn it in less than week. So was the placebo effect of his burning aspiration, that he could succeed in anything that involved becoming a knight. Except for Marp. He felt like he couldn't succeed with Marp, for Marp wasn't an ordinary armor, he was an enchanted armor that was passed down generations by Geoffrey's Lord. The armor itself was a beautiful plate armor encrusted with golden lines and sapphire gems. Runic markings were placed all over the shoulder pieces while the helmet had two eyes drawn on top. Marp refused to ever give an explanation for why he had a squire draw big white circles with little black pupils that gave the helmet an expression of continuous surprise. 'As I was saying! I, Sir Geoffrey of Castle Blackridge 'Dragon!' Marp interrupted him again. The Dragon paced around the rock, attempting to flank Geoffrey and incinerate him completely. There'd be no way for him to survive a full frontal attack. It was a frightening beast, not to Geoffrey of course, but a frightening beast. For the horns that made Geoffrey's legs shake, not from fear but excitement, its mouth that contained a thousand teeth would never make Geoffrey sweat, while its millions or billions of red burning scales definitely did not make Geoffrey run towards the exit. 'Where are you going?' Asked Marp, speaking telepathically to Geoffrey. 'Away from here, tactical retreat!' Sir Geoffrey the Brave screamed. 'Oh no ya don't! I'd rather have you toast inside me than go back to Blackridge.' The armor flung Geoffrey to the side of another rock, avoiding a chunk of boiling spit from the Dragon. 'Are you insane?' Geoffrey asked, still tumbling all over the dirt. 'No! You think I want to be part of another knight? I'm going to be dragged all over the castle as another "brave knight" tries to wear me. It'll be a huge stinking ceremony and I'll be right in the middle of it. If you die, at least I get to be part of a Dragon's treasure, where no one will bother me again.' Marp's logic was sound, but still hurtful. Sir Geoffrey made careful not to think that. 'Think what?' Asked the enchanted armor, it could hear Geoffrey's thoughts. 'Dragon!' Screamed Geoffrey while picking up his sword and sprint past the Dragon's flame breathe incinerating another part of the cave. The flame rammed against the stone wall and ricocheted all over the place. Geoffrey's eyes kept being covered in a waterfall of sweat, he felt his body moving but his legs were numb. The same problem with his arms, they were in the midst of action yet completely gone from his senses. Marp's magic allowed a normal man to survive where he should have died. 'I shall smite thee!' Yelled Sir Geoffrey the Brave at the Dragon, while still running from the Dragon. 'You keep running n' running n' running. Are you going to do something anytime soon?' Marp was losing his patience. He wasn't a fan of noise nor action. 'Like what.' Geoffrey yapped. 'Try stabbing him.' Marp replied. Geoffrey glanced at his sword. 'Stabbing him with this? His scales are akin to plate!' Geoffrey waved his sword around. The Dragon had lost interest in burning Geoffrey, instead it ran towards him, with its wings half-opened and its mouth wide open. Sir Geoffrey felt stiff, he couldn't move at all. Frozen in fear at the gigantic monster about to devour him. 'Oh for God's sake.' Marp groaned. Geoffrey's arms began to move on their own, the enchanted plate armor lifting his sword up before flinging it towards the Dragon's mouth. Making Geoffrey's legs shuffle to the left as he tripped down to the floor, avoiding the attack and being bitten. The Dragon trampled its foot all over the stone floor, trampling Sir Geoffrey a few times. It slammed its head against the wall and wailed a deafening echo throughout the cave system. Blood began to pour from its mouth, down to the floor while the Dragon coughed louder each time. It turned to Sir Geoffrey, giving him a hateful glare before collapsing onto its side, unable to breathe as the sword had gotten stuck in its breathing pipe. Sir Geoffrey groaned and lifted himself off the floor, looking to the Dragon's corpse. 'Congrats, you did it.' Marp spoke sarcastically. 'I did..... I did it!?' Sir Geoffrey the Brave couldn't even believe it. After centuries of the Dragon plaguing Blackridge's population, he had succesfully defeated the tyrant and saved the castle. 'I did it!' Cheered Geoffrey, attempting to jump for a cheer and in a swift moment, feeling as if all of his bones were broken. 'Oh god.' He struggled to stay up, only able to thanks to the armor. 'Yuup.' Marp snickered in his mind. 'Sir Geoffrey!' bellowed out a voice from outside the Cave's entrance. It was Lord Blackridge on his healthy horse, accompanied by his bodyguards and peasants who came to spectate. 'You've defeated the Dragon?' Blackridge said. Geoffrey could sense the incredulous tone in his voice. 'Yes. Say Yes.' Marp told him. 'Yes.' Sir Geoffrey the Brave replied, standing stoically with a pose to add to his spectacle. 'My God! You are truly the best Knight we've had this century.' Geoffrey's heart sank.'The best of this century.... But not of all time?' 'No no, Sir Marvin had defeated a Dragon, and a Hydra. But that was atleast four centuries ago.' Blackridge explained. 'No..... Don't you dare.' Marp growled. 'I shall go defeat the Hydra!' Sir Geoffrey proclaimed, raising his fist into the air. 'Oh, we're going to play it this way, huh?' Marp's voice grew sinister. At that moment, all the magic of the enchanted armor vanished and Sir Geoffrey felt the true pain that he had received from the burns and trampling of the Dragon. He collapsed instantly, to the horror of all the spectators. 'Get him back to Castle Blackridge. He and his enchanted armor will defeat the Hydra!' Lord Blackridge proclaimed, grinning with delight. 'Son of a-!' Marp screamed.

7 more. 4 more. 2 more. Last one. Better. I noticed I was running low on my bottle of pills I had marked "D," so I pulled out my planner and made a note to buy some more. Within 15 minutes, I would be feeling fine, and could go home and enjoy the weekend with my family. It was my first week on the job, and it took an enormous toll. Was it worth it? Absolutely. 10,000 per experience which went directly to my family, and I could get through 2-3 per day before being emotionally wrecked and having to throw in the towel and pop the pills. My week started with what my employer called the "beginner" experience. A wealthy family's dog died my company was paid to experience the pain in place of their daughter. I won't get into too many specifics, for fear of boring you all, but essentially the person who does not want to experience something puts on a helmet, and the helmet copies all of the persons memories about the experience. Then, the employee, myself, takes the helmet and brings it into our lab, where we send in the knowledge of the event happening to the database (in this case we added the information that that dog died). Then, I put on the helmet, and get all of the information, including the unpleasant information. My brain must deal with the pain, and work to get over it to find data on how the memory of the event lives on. We then remove the negative information, and place the helmet back on the client, who learns about life after the experience, but not the negative experience itsself. I went through many different experiences this week, ranging from flunking out of college, to losing loved ones, even as far as one mother who fell asleep driving and crashed into a telephone pole, causing her son to be paralyzed from the waist down. As I packed my things to leave the office, I got a call. I guess the receptionist decided to give me the case that came up 4 minutes before closing since I was new, but I figured why not. I went into her office, opened the package that contained the helmet, and went and sat in our cold, dark, "experience" room. I put the helmet on and hit the begin button on the side. The knowledge I got was nothing short of a horror film. I was experiencing it through the lens of a tall slender women, who kissed a man goodbye and sat in her driveway with her two daughters waving goodbye. The faces were blurred but I could tell the girls and their mother were absolutely gorgeous. As the man went down the road, the 3 went inside where they found 2 men had just broke in through the back door, and were now sitting on the couch. "All your money and jewelry now!" One said more calmly than he should have. The women started backing out of the doorway with her children behind her, when suddenly a shot rang out. A third man had come from behind and shot the youngest girl in the back of the head. This was it. This was what she suffered through. I could feel my palms sweat as I continuously pinched my leg to remind myself this was not actually my life. The woman collapsed screaming, and at that moment was knocked out by the man from behind. When she opened her eyes her house was trashed and the men were on the way out. One leaned down and held took the ring off of her finger. This is when I noticed it. The ring. I had bought that ring. The house looked familiar as it should have with her memories in my head, but I soon identified it as MY HOUSE. The weight of the situation hit me like a ton of bricks. I ripped the helmet off and took off running through our office. By the time I reached my car, I remembered I had turned my cell phone off when I arrived at the office that day. I turned it on, and frantically got in my car. The screen of my phone lit up. 14 missed calls from 911. 4 missed calls from Hope County Memorial Hospital. 1 missed call from the Hope County Morgue.

"I can't believe you've never met him. He talks about you all the time." He sits there, gun in his lap, smiling at me. That cocky smile, the I'm better than you are, and you're completely fucked sort of smile. I try to respond, but of course, when you have tape around your mouth and sack over your head, speaking coherently is an issue. "Really? That's a shame, considering you ruined his life." I feel a sudden breeze hit my face as the bag is ripped from me. We're in an apartment building - one of those New York high rise flats, just been built - empty. The floor to ceiling windows are pushed open. I shiver. My name is Dante; I'm a, well, I WAS a lawyer. I worked for one of the largest law firms in Manhattan, and somehow, after two drinks in my local bar, I ended up here with no memory of current events. None of my clients had ever been called'Sizemore'. The man picks up a picture and thrusts it towards me. I stare at it for a few moments, then blink repeatedly. My heart sinks, and my face too, apparently. He picks up the gun. "Goodbye, Mister Sizemore."

Hank's attention was glued to the pin on the dead man's shirt. He had seen such a pin before, back in college - his friend, then what one would call him, a "hipster," wore it proudly on his plaid jacket. "Eat the rich," the little tin disc said. Eat the rich. His friend's father was a Morgan Stanley analyst, that's how the little shit even got into MIT in the first place. Then again, by the time Hank celebrated his 20th birthday, the notion that the majority of the population suffered a permanent and debilitating, cognitive dissonance, had become old news to him. Amidst the unfolding Mexican standoff, the dead body of the unlucky Purger lay on the oak floor like a demarcating Rubicon. The ragtag team of masked Purgers that managed to break through the automated defense system of Hanks' villa versus three GreyForge mercs (embellished by SWAT, SAS and some Russian inner security), including Hank himself. None dared to cross the line again for the time being. Hank calculated the odds, quickly - four against at least ten, with who knows how many outside in the yard, and automatic weaponry making it all the more unpredictable. Aside from the mortal fear that coiled like a metal mattress spring in his stomach, Hank felt a growing anxiety over the fact that too many incalculable variables were involved. Such unstable systems were his forte as an analyst, but when his own life was at stake, his resolve slowly crumbled under the pressure; the bigger picture fell apart, not letting him think as clearly as he really could. The leader, Chicken Head, pushed forward, a shotgun held confidently at the hip. Something in his lazy gait, in the red, goose-bumped large hands, in the light-brown eyes that Hank still could see under the ridiculous get-up, whispered into his ear with a faint familiarity. Shifting on his tongue like a hair that got stuck to it. "You've heard of me, I think," the man rumbled with a clear Boston accent from within the cockerel rubber mask. "We come to restore justice. Make life a bit more fair. No need to be so inhospitable. People out there want to eat, they need housing, shelter - and fairness, of course..... So few have so much in this country, while so many suffer..... We'll correct that." A man in an Obama mask nodded vigorously by the Chicken Head's side. "Got ta redistribute the wealth, twitchy! Got ta fess up'fore you die!" Hank's lips spread in a wide, shark-like grin that made the contrast shadows under his brow grow deeper, strengthening the similarity with a deep water predator. Sure, he heard of him. The town's two last devastating Purges ripped through the wealthy suburbs, all orchestrated by a particularly clever Purger in a chicken mask - he even managed to build something of a loyal mob in the process. Not like that required some effort, in Hank's eyes - bit of populist slogans, a tiny drop of charisma, and some above average intelligence to keep ahead of your followers. Still, notoriety or not, talk like that never sat well with Hank. Not after what he has been through to get where he was, with this house, these artifacts, these GreyForge grunts. They had no idea and no right. Purge or no Purge, he won't be fed pre-school morals to. Life was not fair, oh yes. Hiring ex-military to survive wasn't among Hank's ideas of life being fair at all. "Spare me the bullshit," he motioned towards the dead man with a gun he got from one of the mercenaries. "Poverty is, for the most part, a social maladaptation, a mix of mental deficiency and purely human desire to brush off responsibility. It's nice to think that someone evil steals you from so that you don't have to face the possibility that maybe it's you who's a pathetic waste of space with nothing to contribute instead!" He chuckled, but his shoulders sagged. Idealism was such a joke. "You, however, are resourceful. Cut the power to my house, managed to shut down and reboot the SafeHouse OS, took the cameras out..... brought a whole mob of welfare leechers, fired up, no less, by a rousing speech on how "the man" owes'em everything for all the'ard work!" Got ta use the Purge to fix "da injustice"!" Hank's mocking tone didn't bode well with the "hardworking masses," eyes glistening menacingly from within the masks, weapons rising. Vladislav, one of the GreyForgers, lay a hand on his boss's chest, trying to push him behind their armored backs, but Hank couldn't help himself. He was tired. He waved his pistol around, accentuating the motion mostly on Chicken Head. "If any of you fuckers ever worked a real job that you earned with your brain and brawn, if your parents were smart people and not drunkards that left you with no capital, but with a shit school and shit education, guess what - maybe you wouldn't be such miserable fuckers, ey? Novel concept, isn't it?" "Shut your trap, pig!" "Yeah, you fucking piece of shit! I'm gon na fucking cut your head off, try to take that to your insurance company, asshole!" "Get him, chief!" Hank held the gun to his face, wiping his nose with the top of the pistol in a nervous tick. He could feel the other man smiling, feeling the power of the mob behind him, rifles, hatchets and axes raised, eager for blood, fueled by misplaced righteousness. The leader was the locus of it all, for certain. "Oh, and your leader! Wonder where he has such profound knowledge of the SH OS, of all my villa's systems, of the type of bots we use for patrol - no, do it! Anyway you spin it - if he worked in the company, if he was a repair man, or - oh my, what a twist! " , Hank's face contorted into a mask of pretend horror. "If he was a customer himself, means that you little rabble-rouser is a capitalist swine himself! Is he not?" Chicken Head shifted on his, his stance changing just a fraction, but it told Hank that his shot was true. It was no disgruntled war vet or an Appalachian farmer raging against social economic inequality during the Bloody Night. No, there was intellect, one that took advantage of free resources without shame. Hank could almost respect that, if his life didn't hang on the line. The police-grade body armor he wore felt paper-thin still. "My men are placing charges under the west wing of your mansion, Mr. Norris," he drawled. "The only thing that's gon na change here, is if you'll be dying quick or slow..... You fellas included. You're outnumbered." Ah. His name, in that voice. Hank's job was to have a good memory, and not just of numbers. His name, in that voice. In a split second, it all clicked into place. Mr. Norris. The Boston accent, the county golf club, the awful lobster-red tan only an Irishman would get, the shreds of a conversation caught in the men's room about hunting trips. Hank licked his lips, and turned his head from one invader to another, from one grinning Purger mask to the other, from one gun barrel to the other. Then, he looked as Fischer, his bodyguard and smiled helplessly, all the previous hardness gone from his face. "See, Fischer, I was right. These folks were duped, and it's a common theme with them. Common root to why they are poor - they let wolves in sheep clothing guide the herd," Hank's face relaxed. "Get ready, we're about to be shot and hacked at." As the GreyForgers tensed, Hank moved behind them, stepping back into the shadow of his home, ready to shoot and flee if his investment into the PMC sector turned out to be a fluke. From behind his bodyguards backs, he called out to the Chicken Head, as the latter pulled a detonator out, about to fulfill the promise to blow half his villa up. "Mr. O'Connor! If you wanted to add that Matisse I got in my vault to your own already impressive collection, you should've just contacted my assistant! Have a chat in the golf club! Not start a bloody proletariat revolution, ey!." Hank remembered the pin, his friend. Well, this was entirely calculable. Someone who can't even make their life tolerable enough to not be an angry piss-stain, wouldn't have come up with such a good plan. But an investment banker? Dog eat dog, Hank thought. Not just the rich.

To finish setup, please enter your product key for McAfee eBrain Anti-Virus and Malware. Are you sure you want to skip this phase? The cover sways with the wind from an open window. Inside it is a yellow page; on the yellow old page are some words; left of the main page has some incorrigible writing pasted onto it as if the writer couldn't be bothered, as if the green ink was poison, as if the inscriber wanted to be done with the task as soon as possible. But I know it is a lie. Whoever it was that has this book before me loved it dearly. How else would I explain the markings, the question marks, the underlines, the different inks, and indecipherable words that lie besides the printed ones, as if they were always there. Every paragraph is adorned with their thoughts. Every yellow old page has those alphabets. The inscriber is the second author here. Their words are my guide.

Goodbye, God, we said and goddamn we meant it. Goodbye, too, brothers and sisters. Friends we never had and enemies we never made. Children's hands we never held and lover's lips we never kissed. The world we left behind is a grey cemetery now. All ghosts we never knew. Like the Polaroid of a long ago vacation in someone else's picture frame. We don't care. Not our God. We're in his Heaven dancing with celestial bodies. We kicked him out of his own party. Man was made to die in the dirt. Well. They wanted to stay down there in their own hell. Serves them right. To Earth is to human.

"Hey," his smile was warm. He outstretched his palm and shook my hand. The pressure was welcoming. I found my lips turning upwards despite myself. They tended to be all the same; the same charming laugh, the same greasy lines, and the same disappointed grin when I left in my car instead of theirs. But this time, the smile I was offered radiated something pure, something very close to naivete. It was endearing, in a way, but I wondered immediately if it was put on. "Hey there," I answered, sitting down. He'd already pulled the chair out for me. Scooting it in, I flicked my eyes once over the menu and decided on what I was going to drink. The same thing I always did: Diet Coke. If he was annoyed, I decided, he was a prick. If he smiled on with those perfect teeth, he wanted to get laid. The waiter arrived before we could say more, asking us what we wanted. "Water," said my date, adding quickly, "with lemon." Classy. Dignified. I opened my mouth to add my little shit-test of a drink order, but he spoke again. "and a cherry." And a cherry. That reminded me of Nana. She always said I should get out there, should talk to boys and fix my hair up. I remembered her slapping my wrist when I grabbed cookies with my hand, soothing my tears with the same snack: water with a maraschino cherry plopped on top of the ice cubes. "When I die," she always said to me, the last time on prom night when she lined my eyes and spun my hair up before I went, before she took a nap and breathed her last. "You'll know I've picked a good man for you'cause he'll know how to make you feel better just the way I do." "Nana," I had laughed at her, "if you're dead, you won't be able to talk to me." I patted the elegant swirl of hair she'd put up for me. Her wrinkly lips quirked up. "Oh, yes I will."

Jordy wakes up in his bunker. Underground, cozy. He stood up and stared at Liss' pink jacket with it's mystical pink ponies and rainbows. The distinct'15' graphic on the back. He missed her more than words can describe at that moment. Tears almost exuded, then retreated. He stares up at the trapdoor almost instinctually. He hears footsteps. He imagined them slumping and lethargic. They always were, until the culling began. A screechy bell rang and jolted Jordy. It was distant yet unmistakeable. It was the church bell being played. The ceremony was beginning. The footsteps stopped, and then Jordy heard it. The bellows of the damned. Screams and frenetic yells. The culling has begun. Jordy sat down with his face against his erect knees and closed his eyes. Time to wait it out.

The party pounded on in the distance, blazing like a far away flare. I walked farther across the backyard, enveloped in thoughts of the future. It was a lovely backyard, big and spacious. It even had a pool, which was, for the most part, unoccupied, except for the lone couple that was drunkenly making out under the diving board. I dragged my feet across the dew covered grass, soaking up the silence. I decided to sit under the nice cover of an oak tree that sat near the outskirts of the yard; it's branches crossing over the other side of the wooden fence. The trunk was sturdy and I lay against it, thinking of everything, letting my mind wander between bliss and sadness, basking in the quiet moonlight of the night, picking grass out of the ground and drawing my name into the dirt. "Shouldn't you be inside, drinking, like the rest of your friends?" whispered a wayward voice from above. My heart jumped against my ribcage and I snapped my neck back, searching for the source of the sound. "Who said that?" I asked, squinting at the dark lattice of branches above me. Suddenly, my eyes settled on a pair of beady red eyes and connected their gaze nervously, "Who are you?" I asked breathlessly. "Don't you recognize me?" said the voice, leaping down in a quick black blur, "I'm your friend." I swallowed hard as the silhouetted figure came into full view. He was tall and human-like, but something was off about him. His hair was a silver white and he had eyes that shifted from red to orange, like firelight. He took a seat next to me in the grass and I could feel heat emanating from him. "Geez," I asked, laughing nervously, "Do you have a fever or something?" "No," he answered, "But I think you might." I stared back at him, half-drunk, and uttered a bewildered, "What?" He laughed, his white teeth gleaming, "I mean. It's a party, what are doing out here, by yourself? Aren't you supposed to be having fun with everyone?" "I could ask you the same question. Besides," I said, looking up at the stars caught between the branches, "I'm having a contemplative moment." He chuckled quietly, "A contemplative moment? What the hell is that supposed to be? "Oh, come on" I said in a slurred surprise, "You know, a moment where you just kind of step back and enjoy the scenery. This beautiful night for instance, where I'm young and everything just feels wrong and right at the same time. And you know it's fleeting, but you're just sort of okay with it..... you know?" "Well, you're quite the thinker," he said simply, "But, yeah, I guess I kind of do." "Cool," I said, "So why the hell were you up in a tree?" "Same thing, you could say." he responded, his shifting eyes, melting into a shade of light orange, "Just observing." "Mmm" "Well," he said, rising to stand, "I should probably get back to that, then." "No," I protested quietly, pulling on his hand, "Stay." He sat back down and I leaned in slowly toward his face, staring at his eyes, feeling his warm breath against mine. Our lips touched for a moment, before, in a black flash he darted away and left me alone. I opened my eyes, my lips still slightly puckered and stared sheepishly at my friend who was standing above me with a look of absolute shock on his face. "Uhh, dude, how drunk are you?" he asked, "There's no one fucking there."

To answer the fist question you'll have, yes. It still hurts. I don't know what caused this. Cellphone radiation, good diet, maybe genetics? Maybe I'll research it. After all, I've got nothing but time now. I think it was a Monday when I first realized that I was..... different. I worked at a gas station in a little town in Arkansas sitting behind the counter. It was a very mundane job, but I enjoyed the quiet. I usually spent my time reading books between the occasional customers I had. One afternoon, just as the sun was beginning to set, I had a customer come in wearing a razorback hat, and a grey sweatshirt. He gave me a weird vibe, so I reached for the shotgun under the counter. I held it in my lap, just out of sight of the man in my store. "Hey man, mind if I get a pack of Camel Reds?" He spoke with an odd kindness that alleviated my anxiety. I set the gun down and turned towards the rack of cigarettes behind me. When I turned back I was looking down the barrel of a gun. I was expecting him to ask me to open the register or something, but all I heard was a loud bang. I screamed like a little kid and pulled my arms in front of my face. There were a few moments of silence before the man ran out of the store. I lowered my arms with one eye squinted. He was gone. I just thought I was the luckiest bastard alive, which in retrospect, I guess I wasn't exactly wrong. I went back into the employee bathroom to wash the sweat off my face, but the mirror greeted me with a gruesome figure. Part of my head was missing. I was in shock. I sat on the floor looking into the mirror for an hour trying to contemplate my situation as I watched my head slowly heal. My first thought was I could heal fast like some character out of a comic book. To test that theory, I left the station and drove to the highway overpass. It took an hour or two to coax myself into jumping, but I eventually worked up the courage. I fell to the hard asphalt below. Jesus Christ did that hurt. I had to of broken a dozen bones, and crushed a few of my internal organs. I had to learn more about this new found gift of mine. I never went back to work. The next couple of months were spent testing the extent of my ability. I tried not eating for a couple of weeks. I felt hungry, but nothing more. I tried fire next. Holy shit that was a mistake. I burned the skin off my body entirely and my nerves screamed with pain. That was when I learned the extent of my healing. I heal at the same rate as other normal people except for fatal injuries. Gunshot to the head took about an hour, spike in the heart took two, broken neck took about a day. I spent my days doing all the things I wanted to do. I travelled mostly, and I read a lot. As the years went by, I started to notice my family got older and died, while I stayed the same age. That is what confuses me the most I think. Why did I stop aging that day? Maybe I was always immortal, but that doesn't explain why I aged at all. Then again, I don't have much of a mind for science. I realized my amazing gift was actually a terrible curse. I had to watch everything die around me as I stood still, frozen in time. It's a lonely life I live, but I still try to make the most of it.

First time, please don't hate it. I always understood love hate relationships because of cleaning. Cleaning my home was the only thing that caused both emotions. Running? Love. Painting my nephew's room a terrible color because my sister-in-law wants it? Hate. My nephew? Love. Cleaning was an evil I did with excitement for the result, which was a version of my home I expect to see in the new heaven and earth. Every year I sweep everything, floor, scrub every tile, check all my clothes, and rearrange my bookshelf. Finally finished with my bachelor's of communications, I realized I would almost certainly never need those textbooks again. Here's like... almost a thousand dollars in paper paperweight I thought, rather fond of the " paper paperweights " oxymoron. Finding yet another paper based product in the garage (cardboard box), I loaded the textbooks in and headed upstairs. The hallway has a rather unassuming attic entrance towards the far end, and I've never before made an excuse to go up. My jobs paid for tuition instead of enough crap to need an attic. Great, the dust from opening the door is gon na make me sweep again. The light of course, had not worked since the Soviets were a threat, and the free flashlight from my credit union illuminated only a few degrees, despite its bulk on my key ring. I set the box of communication methods down in some random corner that was unlikely to make it a tripping hazard and was about to turn the pitiful fluorescents off when I saw a box directly behind the door, supporting it from slamming against the floor. Not wanting to close myself in the attic, I managed to drag it down the ladder into the hall with one arm. It was a light box, but unusually large. The corrugated brown paper was so old, it disintegrated instead of ripping open, brown dust settling on the contents, covering the triangle left somewhat intact in my palm. The dust settled and I thought there was some encyclopedia taking the entirety of the box. There aren't any ridges between volumes. I ended up flipping the box upside down, breaking the other side in, and pushing the book out from the edges where it was until just recently snugly ensconced. It must have been a 2 by three feet, at least, but it wasn't very thick, maybe about the size of a Bible. The brown cardboard dust matched the actual cover almost perfectly, and would have remained unnoticed had not the angled light betrayed shadows splaying across the world. I was so thoroughly confused by the thing, and I thought it was the odd size of it until I realized it was blank. Just... entirely blank. No author. No title. No publisher or year, or anything except for the text that made the bulk of the pages. And the first page made no sense whatsoever. I couldn't begin to understand it, the characters were entirely alien to me, with a stark, beautiful contrast between straight, thick lines, and thin hairpin curves. It was like two distinct people had to have written half of each symbol. As I flipped through, the characters blended, becoming more uniform, evolving. By the middle of the volume, it was something Asian, but still not anything I could understand. By page 509, there were smatterings of Latin, or Greek, or French, which I understood. Names and events I could translate, but it didn't make sense for another 40 pages, until most of the entries were in modern languages. " Francis Cassavant - November 26, 1947. Suicide because of guilt, war, and anger. " A name, a date, and a cause of death. Over and over the pattern emerged, becoming more frequent than the ones I could not understand or translate easily with my phone. Was every entry like this? I was shocked. I kept turning pages, but the sensation of the aged paper crackling and escaping my fingers became numbed. The names and dates were nothing, but the causes were all bleak. The most natural cause of death became a tragedy with a few simple words added on to it. " Arthur Glennon - Dec 25 1999. Aborted in second trimester. Would have taught English at MIT. " The dates are getting closer and closer. I feared how recently this book might have been edited. I moved in 5 months ago, so the list stops before March of 2011, right? They didn't. At least a hundred thousand people died today. And it kept going, into tomorrow, and next week and year and decades. My name is in this. I knew it must be. I didn't care about the logic of a book predicting fate, I had already seen entries for people I knew. The teacher in middle school who died of cancer. The uncle who took me hunting for the first time, and carried the kill because I couldn't even lift him. Hours after dragging the cardboard coffin down, I found what I was looking for. " Andrew Clemente - August 1 2040. Car crash with semi - at fault. " Right below were 2 other English entires. " Ally Clemente - August 1, 2040. Car crash. " " Andrew Clemente II - August 1, 20104. Car crash. " I was shaking and crying. I hadn't even met this Ally yet, and now I didn't want to. I never want to see her, or my son, because I know that I will by their undoing. I don't care about the joy of marriage or fatherhood. And I kept telling myself this. Every day I would renew a vow to not fall for Ally, to not be married or have a son, but every spring I check and the names don't change or go away. Every day I think that I'm going to live the rest of my life unhappy, because I know I hurt the people I'll one day love the most.

Aurelie looked out of the window onto the sprawling mess of metal trees that was the city. Such serenity for a Monday. Her tea was the perfect temperature to sip, and the rain came down softly onto the tops of the skyscrapers, where the filters gurgled to pump the water through the pipes. The cashmere of her sweater enveloped her as she became lost in thought. The legislation to deregulate business using the labor from below was coming along nicely. Today they were going to pass some new bills for bathroom breaks. Silly how such a thing could have an impact on worker productivity. Not nearly as important as minimum wage, which was a bigger battle. She didn't notice Pollux's soft hand on her shoulder until it came up to stroke her cheek. " It's time. You're needed, " he said, giving her a gentle kiss. " Good luck. " " Of course I am. " Her high heels clacked on the marble floor. She quickly applied some lipstick in the mirror of the foyer. Now she was the perfect chairwoman. At peace. Contained. Whole. She stepped out of her door and into chaos. Men and women were rushing every which way, whispering in an urgent panic. She took the elevator up and inquired what was going on. " They're coming, " said her secretary. " The people from below. They're coming up. " Aurelie laughed. " Excellent.
