At the age of 56, Doctor Graham Chadford's death came as a shock to the small village of Sumperton. He had been at the last parish meeting less than a week before, and nobody there thought there was anything remotely wrong with his health. Word quickly got around the village of his passing, and hundreds sent their condolences to his son Andrew, his only heir. Andrew was not even thirty, and he had already lost both of his parents. He had died in hospital, following a heart attack in his own GP office. It was a sudden heart attack, midway through treating a patient. The patient in question ran for help as soon as he realised, and Graham was quickly taken to hospital. A second heart attack followed in the middle of the night, this one proved fatal. Dr Chadford was well respected in the village. He was the main GP and served not only all Sumperton, but also patients from villages nearby. He was a well respected member of the community, listed as a member of the local parish council, and involved in many community activities, from successfully petitioning the prevention of a city bi-pass that would've gone right through Sumperton, to assisting with the replanting of hundreds of new trees in after a strong storm battered the area causing thousands in damages. He even personally paid for some of those who had lost their homes to stay in hotels while they got their property sorted, and while the local council (grudgingly) reimbursed him, he said he would've done it either way. The Chadford's were quite well off. Graham's late wife was an inventor, and held patents for a small device that was almost ubiquitous in any kitchen. The pair often joked they could retire at any point, and spent a small part of their fortune building their own home from the ground up, and over the years they had dozens of contractors in constantly making improvements and small changes, from double glazing and soundproofing, to extensions and a side garage. It was a lovely home, and one that suited the three of them to a tee. Graham Chadford was well respected as a doctor. He had published numerous medical journals, on a wide variety of topics to do with patient care. The medical community had made note of his work, citing one particular paper on the ways to to ensure correct sustenance for patients who were unable or, unwilling to eat as ground breaking. His career started with him as a big city hospital doctor, but he soon found he preferred life in the country and when a GP's position opened up he leaped at the chance. Of course, many who had known him for a long time would tell you this was him trying to repent. After the death of his wife some twenty years ago Graham had started drinking heavily. He struggled to cope with the loss of his wife Lorraine, and lashed out at anyone who tried to help him. He very nearly lost his medical license, and it was only through an intervention from some of his closest friends that he finally decided to sort himself out. Andrew Chadford said at his funeral that although his father had made some mistakes, his father had redeemed himself in the eyes of many. Andrew tearfully spoke of a father who simply tried his best, and while not perfect, his father had always made it clear that he loved his son more than anything. It took Andrew a couple of weeks to clear out his fathers house. He had put it off at first to grieve, but then relented and accepted he had to do it. Andrew took his time sorting through the possessions, finding souvenirs and photos of family holidays, old wedding albums, even some of Andrew's old drawings from when he was little. But the biggest surprise was in the basement, where, in a sealed up room, was stored a very skinny woman in her mid thirties, a woman who had been tied to the wall and fed through a tube her whole life.

France, July 1916 We've been losing junior officers nearly every day now. The new second lieutenant won't last long. Although he seems to keep his head down, so perhaps he'll do better than the others. He doesn't want to be here. None of us want to be here. I can't even picture what it's like in the forward trenches, it's bad enough back here. We're no more than a mile from the worst and we still do have to be on our toes. I hardly think any of us will survive. I'm trying to record everything but I'm tasked with keeping a look out most of the time. The lieutenant on the other hand keeps his nose in the books. He showed me a poem he's been working on, after some pestering on my behalf. It's an interesting piece about the journey over here. I'd like to see it when it's finished. He's allowed me to call him John when we're alone. Sometimes we talk about things not of this world. Anything to pass the time or take the mind off the worst. I asked him what it would be like if one of us found our way to these imagined lands. I believe it wouldn't be much unlike traveling to a foreign land. You'd have trouble with the language of course, perhaps even the alphabet or whatever they used. Customs would be barbaric if not downright unintelligible. Oh but the lieutenant had to make it really strange. He imagined the folk to be tall and lithe, living forever. What a lonely island that would be. Everyone lives forever? I suppose there would be no conflict, right? I'm having trouble picturing this place but it seems very firm in his imagination. It's time to move. I shall write later. -Tommy Atkins EDIT: typos, clarity and repetition.

Hannah was the weird one in our class, she always sat in the back staring into space, it was so strange, she never interacted with anyone, just sat there staring or doodling weird things like knives, eyes and scars. She was just bizarre and she was our target, we all did it pulling pranks on her, chucking food at her, chasing her around school, name calling. The rumours about how she was a devil worshipper, how she killed cats, drank her own blood, all manner of gruesome things; everyone knew it was bullshit but we still kept at it. Some days when we were really bored we'd all start on her, chase her around school until we caught up with her, we'd pull out her hair till her scalp was all bloody, blacked her eyes till she couldn't see, stamped on her hands till her fingers broke and hit her until her ribs cracked. It was all fun though and she knew it, she never reacted, never hit back she even smiled during it, it was all fun and games. . Dear Diary, Today's been a good day and it wasn't too bad today at school, I only got called names and spat at. The name calling is funny though; they accused me of sacrificing cats, how stupid could they be? They really think people do that, it's so silly. The spitting is worse though because I might as well be shit on the floor with how they treat me. Mum isn't too bad either today which is a nice change, she was asleep when I got in so it was up to me to tidy up and cook dinner before Dad got home, he came back happy, I like them nights because he usually leaves me alone but he's coming upstairs now so I better go. Love you lots, Hannah. xx Dear Diary, I spoke to soon last night when I said it was a good day, dad was to happy last night but it's okay because I went to my castle in the sky, I watched the stars drift past the sky and even saw a few shooting stars so it wasn't all too bad. School was more entertaining today I was chased around for all of lunch in my field of daisies, I didn't even realise my nose was broken until I went to the bathroom. Snapping it back into place and cleaning the blood up was no problem, it's the stain on the shirt I was worried about, mum would go ballistic when she saw it and that's what she did. She screamed and shouted at me when I got back, she must have been in pain and she is always her worse when she's in pain. She ripped my blouse off and sent me to my room, finally the tears came today, it had been horrible but at least I had rusty, my best friend, he makes everything better and tonight dad didn't come home. Love you, Hannah X Dear Diary, The weekend was fun; I just spent it up in my room reading while the rain pelted down the window, have you ever noticed how relaxing the sound of rain is? It's always my favourite night when I can drift off to the rain which came in handy this weekend since dad visited me a few times, I wish he wouldn't because mum always blames me even though I never did anything wrong but my nose is healing now which is good. Today we had P.E, it always my favourite lesson especially the changing rooms, I always sneak into the bathroom to get changed I don't want people see disgusting body, not that they don't remind me off that enough, how fat and ugly I am. It's almost like they don't know that I know, is there any need to remind me? I don't think so. Lucky me it was rounder's today, everyone's favourite game as it's how many times can you hit Hannah with the ball with an extra ten points for hitting me in the head. The rest of the day was relatively quiet another run around my field of daisies but nothing broken today! I would call that a rather productive day at school. Home was another thing though, mum has had enough of my shit as she calls it, so no food, no clothes, no shower, she even took the mattress out of my room but the floor is comfier anyways so it doesn't bother me too much. Later when dad came home he called me down so they could take turns in using me as their personal punch bag but after all that rusty came round to help calm me down. He is the bestest friend anyone could ask for. Love, Hannah xx Dear Diary, Sorry I didn't write yesterday but I'm off school today so we can catch up. I went to school aching from the night before, every bit of me was sore and everyone at school laughed when they saw me and that stung. They didn't even bother chasing me today, just ambushed me after school, dragging me by my hair into the woods behind the school, I was finally free but they grabbed another clump of my hair not realising the first one had just been ripped out. They hurt me. They hurt me so bad. I can't even remember what happened, one minute I was being dragged into the woods the next I was just lying in my own blood, I couldn't even find my clothes or bag, all I wanted to do was go home but I couldn't, what if people saw me? I couldn't let people see me so I stayed there until it was dark out before I ran home. It only got worse, mum was in pain, dad was drunk so it was back to my castle in the sky for the second time that day. I can't take it anymore, Rusty is telling me I should get Brandy and Charlie to make myself feel better but I'm not sure even though it's very tempting. I'm not at school today because I can't move, it could be because I'm in too much pain, it could be because I was shackled to the garage wall all day and just my joy dad was at home to, now I'm in even more pain and there's nothing I can do other then fly away to my castle in the sky. Goodbye, Hannah. Xx . Hannah McKenna was found five months later, she was barely recognizable. She had been missing patches of hair and scalp from her head and sustained second degree burns on her arms and face, she had suffered from numerous sexual assaults before and after death causing extensive damage to her vaginal and anal cavities. She had been contorted into an odd position so she could fit under the floor boards of her bedroom helped by the fact that her rib cage had been completely caved in, broken legs and snapped vertebrae. The police had only become aware of her disappearance after the school board tried to get into contact with her family for long term absence. Cause of Death; Overdose from a cocktail of alcohol and prescription drugs. . No-one ever gave two thoughts about Hannah, she was our play thing, our toy to keep ourselves amused, to take away our pain from our own lives and put it on her. If I knew, if I knew I wouldn't have done what I had done and now I will always be wrecked from grief, from guilt for what I did to her.

She came back inside ten minutes after she'd left; two minutes after the rain started. She dripped all over the hardwood floor and didn't think twice about throwing herself into me. "What happened?" I ask. She wraps her legs around me, then her arms close behind my neck. "It started raining then these dogs started chasing me and I had to run really fast and now I'm full of adrenaline so just shut up and kiss me." She gives me that look. Hair spilling everywhere, all sunshine and shivers I push her against the wall of our tiny apartment. She runs small hands through my hair and squeezes her legs around my waist. Starts unbuttoning my shirt. We're really making up this time. It starts pouring and I can't make her out from the rain. I carry her into our tiny bedroom and fall on top of her and the bed. We roll over. She's on top now. I grab her back and slide her shirt off, letting it drop on the floor in a wet pile next to her backpack. She presses her skin against mine. The rain picks up and now she's kissing me, her hands warm as she pulls my hair. I grab her waist and rock her back and forth; she begins the motion on her own and I move up to her bra. It's after the storm. I'm laying in bed, she's outside smoking a cigarette on our excuse of a balcony. She says the sky turned purple on account of the rain. I tell her it's us, painted across the evening sky and that someone should make a song about it, make a song about her. She laughs and asks me if I've even seen the clouds that color before. I walk outside and see the mess we made, indigo and all over the place. "Not until tonight."

I gazed at the clock. Thirty degrees had passed since I last checked and I was beginning to sense the repetition set in. I was surrounded by all this junk, these shards of metal and splinters of bone. Billions of years ago there were great lizards stalking the earth, they died out shortly after. In their remains we found bubbles, smaller than anyone could imagine, trapped beneath the sun bleached tomb. Afterwards there were creatures much like us, but different in a few ways. For one they must have had feathers like the great lizards, being the stepping stone between us and them. We discovered they were called humans. Regardless they also died out shortly after. We thought nothing of it, until I found more bubbles in their skeletons. That's my job, you see, I try to figure out what the hell came before us. That was until recently, now my job is to find out what killed the lizards and the humans before it kills us. The death was a cycle, all life on this planet must have fallen to it had they survived all else. I was sitting in this room knowing that at any moment, an incredibly precise one that I know nothing about, my family might die. I must stop what is coming to is. It's just so tedious. I gazed at the clock, thirty four degrees had passed.

Bill was not a rich man. But he was a nice man. For as long as Bill could remember he had done his job perfectly. It wasn't a hard job so that wasnt saying much. However, Bill managed to feel happiness in his performance. And so Bill was happy. Bill stood at an impressive 1 and half inch, almost a giant for his kind. He had a rugged look to him, a fact that was mostly due to him hardly ever shaving. Now, this isn't to say he was a mean, imposing man. Oh no, Bill was renown throughout the Hollow as a kindly elder gentleman. Those who had met the man face to face (and few there were) said that his eyes, when locked onto yours, seemed to peer deeply into your soul. They said it was almost as if he could read your mind. Now, everyone knew that stuff such as "mind-reading" was a ridiculous concept so most everyone tok this as just another urban legend surrounding the old man. But, back to Bill. You see, tonight was Bill's last night on the job. After serving faithfully for two-hundred and thirty-six years Bill would finally be done. Those around him who knew him would all agree when it was said that he deserved this retirement. And those who worked with him even accredited him as being "the best in his field." Bill should have been ecstatic. The retirement plan for his line of work was phenomenal. The forms he had filled out two-hundred and thirty-six years ago had promised that he would live the rest of his life comfortably, surrounded by as much honey and bee legs as he wanted. But as Bill sat on the end of his bed and looked around his small Comb he understood something. Bill realized that he loved his job. he didn't want to quit now, to stop going to work. The laid back life didn't and would never suit someone like Bill. But seeing as the TCA, or Tooth Collection Agency, would refuse to let him go out any more after tonight he needed to figure out a plan. The night passed without much huzzah. Bill had returned that morning to the TCA with a record number of teeth and was congratulated accordingly. But as Bill returned to his Comb for the last time he looked down inside his standard issue brown overcoat. Inside sat nestled a shiny white tooth. In in the sub-standard lighting of his Hive it was easy to tell that Bill had brought home a VERY high quality tooth. He went inside and set it on his lone red reclining chair then went to bed. Bill had a busy day tomorrow and needed a good nights rest. Weeks would pass. Bill's Comb had long since been abandoned and even though no one there really knew him, it was said that he was missed. Bill had moved three Hives higher. His Comb now had not only consistent water flow but also decent natural lighting. But Bill was hardly ever home so he never really took notice of these minute details. Bill was now a rich man. He had everything a normal fairy would ever want in life. But it hadn't been enough for him. Going out at night, feeling the rush as he delicately traded out a tooth for several shiny coins, experiencing the soft breeze on his wings. Bill just couldn't give it up. So he didn't. In his long life Bill had made many "connections." The legality of said connections was always open to debate and the societies within which these connections roamed were always under inspection by the TCA. So when Bill had shown up at one of their secretive hide-outs it had come as a huge surprise for everyone there. He was greeted hostilely at first but after a few drinks and stories from Bill everyone agreed that he was an "Okay guy." Larry was his name. Larry was an ex-TCA like Bill and they had met in the line of duty. Their shared passion for tooth-hunting is what led them together in the end. They became close friends from that night forward and they were never seen separate. Teeth were important. They always were and it seemed they would continue to be. But you see, teeth never had any real value. They never did. No one knew who had started the rumor that "teeth have massive value" but the government let it continue. The ruling government at the time, the "Faepublican Party" had seen it as a perfect opportunity to give fairies something to do. A way to further control the population. So they established the TCA to help further the illusion. In truth, all the teeth received by the TCA were burned to ash. But Bill didn't know this. And Larry didn't know this. But it was an important job that they both did now, at least to them. Sneaking off late at night to trade in teeth without permission from the TCA was punishable by three-hundred and twenty-one years in the Web. But Bill and Larry didn't care. Teeth were never important. But teeth provided purpose. And purpose made Bill happy. Happy.

Day 27- Expedition to Pregla Island. It's been almost a month since we landed on Pregla. Our team had heard of strange sightings here dating back to the Stone Age. We came here to expose whatever it was that inhabited the island. What we found here will change the world. Last night we reached our destination. A temple that many sailors had seen before. They said that once a man enters, he can never return. We were going to enter the abyss. It was a huge massive structure and oddly it looked made of metal but in the shapes of stones. I took a deep breath and told my companions that this part is not mandatory. I however will be going in regardless. A few chickened out but they also could keep watch from the other side. Elizabeth and Ollie joined me on the venture. We began to walk though the temple. A weird line marked the floor and glee like it had some sort of bioluminescence. We followed it until we reach a gate. The door was oddly marked in thousands of languages. Japanese, German and finally English. "The Operators of Atlantis." We were puzzled but decided it was time to see what was behind the door. Elizabeth pushed it open. What we saw was amazing. Gigantic temples made of metal, flying cars and robots. It was as if a portal to another world. Then we saw a sign, "Atlantis Founded 33 BC.

When they came it all changed. People who vowed to be our protectors, would also be our downfall. They looked down on us, like we were children. They were arrogant and we loathed them. We had rebellions, sure, and thats why theres only a population of 100 million circle jerkers of the angel worshippers. Most of us wouldn't admit it, but we want them gone. Bad. One divine being also came with them, in the shadows. He never spoke, and was always hidden. Sometimes he would be caught by the angels, only to drift away in a puff of smoke. Few, if any, had seen his face. His body showed that he was, very weak, the little times he spoke his voice was quiet and hoarse. Even at his weak state, he appeared a better version of all the angels individually. He was cryptically in support of all the rebellions that went on through the years, never making any direct contact. He's a celebrity, he's famous for the humans and infamous to the angels. The enemy of my enemy is my friend, I suppose. Through the decades, the old being grew a liking and respect to humanity. The last rebellion that claimed 1 billion lives (1 billion humans, 0 angels) he erected a monument. Most people adored it, it was really something beautiful. Something that reminded us of time before the fighting and the "protectors." The 1 angel true worshippers defaced it. Soon after the angels took it down, people go there once a year and stand in a moment of silence. The old being had been in hiding since the angels took it down. People have looked far and wide for him, and even I. It took me 12 years to search the world for him. I lost the one I loved most to the war that had claimed so many lives. I vowed revenge on the angels. He's a good place to start. I found him in an abandoned castle sitting on the throne. He appeared to have not moved in a while, dust had claimed his body. He knew I was there though, and sat up. "Hello?" I said The figure did not speak, he appeared more worse for wear since people last saw him. His wings, they appeared to be broken. Every few seconds he would uncontrollably fade into smoke, only to come back again. He appeared to be very in pain. "Please, don't go, have a seat." He was delighted to hear, and sprang to life for a brief moment. He sat down "May I ask who you are?" This time, he spoke. "I am..... lucifer" he said, his voice seemed so hopeless. It appeared he had simply given up. "Hello lucifer, I need your help" "NO!" he said and got up immediately "The angels can not be stopped!" his voice shook the whole castle "Ive tried too many times and lost count" "I lost allies, fallen ones I held so dear." "What do you mean?" "A long time ago, I used to be the most powerful angel in all the land. My pride and ambition soon got the better of me, and I rebelled for power. Me and the comrades I had made fell into a pit of burning brimstone. It did not take long for them to 1 by 1 become a shell of their former self. They were simply too weak, I however, prevailed as the sole survivor of that tragedy. When the angels came, so did I, through some sort of loophole in design they had constructed" "I was weak yeah, but strong enough to make them notice I was here. They hunted me down, failing due to humanity's continued rebellion." "I had supported them, spending time in the pit made me reflect on who I am." "I constructed the monument in my own image, before the pride and ambition. I hope He would see it. He probably ignored it though." "Who's he" I asked. "The leader of the angels, that had left me in the pit" You could see him even mentioning the pit brought about some sort of slight ptsd episode, he was a very traumatized being. "So then?" "Once the monument was destroyed, he did not want me here. He thought I had gained power, and wanted me banished yet again. I fled here, where I battled. I used all the strength to fight them back." I saw the wounds, the broken wings, the blood all around the place. "I want the angels out just as much as you do" he said "But I am the most powerful being on your side right now, and thats not saying much" "I feel like my comrades felt, before they perished." The few second uncontrollable fade became worse after that. "Can I see your face?" I asked He revealed himself, his face burned to the core, and he appeared to be slightly crying. He had 2 horns, they both however broke off. His pupils which probably once were fiery red, now looked like ash. He walked to me, and patted me on the back. We stood there, me in awe of his figure. Soon, he decayed. "It's happening" he cried, I saw a red little star come out of his body. The star appeared like a red giant star, nearing the end of its lifespan. Soon, it collapsed in on itself. The remaining fragmented star he gave me. "A gift, my only friend left" "Be the man..I once was" "and don't be who I became" After that, his body turned to stone. It aged and crumbled in a matter of seconds. I took the bits of stone to the old monument, and built a grave. I remembered the strange being until I soon passed away, I had tried and failed to build another rebellion once. Nobody's soul was in it no more. Soon, even people started to dwindle due to the maltreatment they received. I was one of, if not the last, one to perish. The angels looked at me, as I looked at the being's soul "I'm sorry" I said to him "I failed" I laid on the grave of that man, instead of dying I became more powerful. I had absorbed his soul. I had poofed away, the angels thought I was gon na die. I did too. Instead this happened. "We will get our vengeance" He spoke I instantly arrived at the old castle, my body flourished in red. Wings sprouted, bigger than the old mans. The pupil was not a pupil, it was the soul of the being. We sat down on our lonely throne, and plotted to rid the universe of the divine and arrogant beings.

He looks well off. Brown overcoat, black leather shoes, combed hair, and square glasses with silver frames. The crowd is flowing around us, but I see only him. There's a hook between my knuckles. I flow behind him, matching his pace, moving with him, and the crowd. The hook swings into his pocket. I give it a light tug and it catches something. A little more and a plastic envelope starts to peek out. Wonder what's inside. It falls from his pocket and dangles from the line and I wrap the tether around my wrist and pull it in. He doesn't feel a thing, just keeps walking. I turn and head in the opposite direction. The envelopes secured with some sort of adhesive. It doesn't take long to peel the top off. There's a vial inside, I take it out and throw the envelope away. I hold it up to the light from the street lamp. The liquid inside is a pale translucent blue. I wrap my hand around it and keep walking. There's a drunk just a little ahead of me, leaning too far when he walks. I get near and he bumps my hand. The vial cracks and cuts me a bit, spilling the liquid into the cut. It burns, and I drop the vial. The skin around my hand starts to blister. The cut turns yellow and swells outward. I close my hand, put it in my pocket and start running. People moving around me, both directions. I have to get out, I have to leave, but I don't have time. I wretch into the crowd, most of it hits a blond lady. A bit of the spray peppers the people around her. She shakes her hands in the air and screams. I run past her, then my legs give. I fall to my knees. Everything starts spinning, the skin on her face starts blistering and she screams louder. I fall back into darkness.

"Oh, honey..." The doll Ashley held in her grip did have tear stains. I pried it from her fingers, which slowly lost their resistance as the tears poured faster and faster off Ashley's face. It hurt to look at, but I checked her neck. The bruises were starting to heal, slowly, but for now they remained ugly purple marks on my beautiful daughter. I read to her while we waited, and she fell into an uneasy sleep. My phone buzzed. I went to the front door, where Eric, the neighbor's son, stood. "She's already asleep. Just..... watch her, and let me know if anything comes up." He nodded solemnly, eyes wide. I knew he was probably wondering what was wrong with us, measuring just how broken we were. I left my house, angry thoughts surrounding me, walking to visit my wife in jail.

"Target hit, I repeat target hit" called our communications tech over the radio. "Do we have eyes on the target." I asked walking over to the computer screen in the middle of the room. "Yes sir, we will have satellite image in 5..4..... 3..... 2..... 1. Putting image on main screen" said the ensign. The entire room stopped what they were doing to look at the TV. No one breathed as we all waited for the smoke to clear from the blast sight. As the smoke dispersed a deafening cheer filled the room, people got up and started to hug each other. "Calm down were not done yet. In fact im pretty sure this is only the beginning." On screen was an alien world, its red sands turned to glass as its towers crumbled to the ground. It had been years of work and trial but we were finally able to fight back. Soon we would take the fight back to them, we would reclaim our world.

" Oh god, that was probably a bad idea. " I thought to myself as I did my best totally-not-drunk walk into the office. Why would I schedule an interview right after my business date with Mr. Johnson from Corporation, LLC., really?! Five drinks had turned into fifteen and..... urgh, no use worrying about the past..... My interviewer sat on the far side of a mahogany desk, her long black hair draped over her shoulder, her brown eyes catching the light streaming in through the window, her blouse stretching as she turned to face m NO! Bad Brian! I had to remain professional! I sat in the chair across from her. I could get through one interview. I smiled, and she flipped the pages of what I assumed to be my resume. "Pleasure to have this meeting, Mr. Campbell," she began, "but as you can assume, you have extensive competition for entering this field." Oh, yeah, I had figured. I couldn't have been the only guy going for a position this..... attractive. But I guess that's why I did have a date just before. "So, Mr. Campbell, I'm going to have to go over quite a few categories in this interview. Previous position experience?" "Missionary, cowgirl, reverse cowgirl..." I began to list off, but she cut me off. "I was referring to experience in the position of Boyfriend, Mr. Campbell," she explained. I caught a glimpse of a smirk, though. She couldn't hide that from me. "Oh yes, of course." I cleared my throat. "Two previous relationships, both between five and six months in length and both within the last five years. Both ended semi-amicably over monetary issues." I covered my mouth as a small hiccup escaped. How could I have let Mr. Johnson talk me into that much alcohol?! "Well, Mr. Campbell," she sighed, rolling back in her chair. "While your (ahem) physical talents and experiences fulfill the requested requirements, your history of relationships ending based on your income..." "Actually," I interrupted, "I have one quick amendment to make to my resume. As of next week, I will be making a six-figure salary." I grinned like a buzzed lunatic and her coy smirk came back. Oh, yeah, that's why I let Mr. Johnson talk me into that much alcohol. First post, please be gentle!

"Is there a reason why?" I ask "Nothing specific, I've just always had this urge, and I had to tell somebody. I knew I could tell you, you're my best friend right?" "Of course I am man. Your secret is safe with me." Brad left the house and I felt an eagerness to follow him. I had too. He couldn't do this by himself, he's lost, he needs me. By the time I got in my car Brad was half way down the road and I followed. It was dark, I knew he couldn't see my car, my headlights yes. But there's no way he could tell it was me. The longer we drove the more eager I became. My toes begin to wiggle and my fingers begin to tap. Thoughts in my head are running rapid. I can't believe I'm following a potential murderer. Eventually he parks, I turn off my headlights and sit there, I'm a decent ways away, no way he could see me. Then he goes inside with a box. Jesus Christ, I figured he would just put a bullet to his head and be done with it. I begin to walk up to the place he entered, I peek through the window and see a man strapped to a chair with plastic laid all around. He's crying. My teeth are grinding. I can't wait anymore. I barge in through the front door and Brad jumps. "What the fuck are you doing here?" He asks I stare right at him and take the box and open it. I toss him a knife and pick one out for myself. "We're best friends right?"

The room is clean and mostly empty. It is cold. My bare feet feel like ice on the linoleum floor. Goosebumps raise the hair on my arms and legs. My gown barely covers my backside. There is a metal table with a device reminiscent of a dentist chair light. There is a large two way mirror on the opposite side of the room. I look at my 32 year old reflection for the last time for the next 15 years. "Please lay down flat on the table," a voice says through the intercom. As I lay down I can't help but shiver. "It's very cold in here." "The temperature of the room is very important to the procedure. It is imperative that you did not bring in any materials other than the gown we provided to you." The man on the intercom is Dr. Rockwell. He recruited me into the program as I am a unique candidate. Dr. Rockwell had been a physics teacher at my high school who got issued a government grant to bring his theory on retrocausality to experimentation. Dr. Rockwell believes without a doubt that physical time travel is a complete impossibility since matter itself can not be created or destroyed, at least in the conventional sense. He believes that physically traveling through time must replace the matter that existed at that time, without a medium for that to occur it can never be accomplished. However, it was his genius that came up the the Flashback Program. Just because matter can not travel across time does not mean that information can not. My job was to test his theory. Since I knew Dr. Rockwell 15 years ago. I was to approach him and accelerate his program. Of course, at first it didn't make sense to me. Why would he send me back in time when he could just go himself. He is a whole lot smarter than I will ever be. Risks are involved with the program and I unfortunately have been diagnosed with lung cancer and told I have just another year or two of life left; who wouldn't jump at the chance to travel back and stop themselves from smoking in the first place? I didn't really have much to risk, I am childless and single with no family of my own to speak for. "No, I have not brought anything in with me." Before entering into the room I was told to take a hot shower and scrape every part of my body with a rather rough pumice to clear all dead skin and possible contaminates from my body. The gown was pulled out of a shrinkwrapped package immediately after exiting the shower just outside the room. "Good, then we shall begin," The intercom clicked off and the device now over my head now lit up. A whirring noise started to hum softly at first then became almost deafening. I wanted to cover my ears but I had been told to lay completely still during the process. The whirring softened again and the light dimmed but did not completely turn off. The intercom clicked again and Dr. Rockwell spoke, "Alright, the device has been calibrated. Remember, you will be our first chrononaut. If all goes well together you and I will change the world. Do you remember the password?" When Dr. Rockwell first thought of this experiment he had the foresight to think of a password if he ever did get to fulfill his dream. I responded with the word he had given me, "Conundrum." "Good luck," I heard the click of the intercom one last time before there was a loud bang and bright flash of light. The next thing I know I am laying face down into a pillow. I open my eyes and I see the sheets are a plaid green. I am having trouble moving at first. I was told that this could be disorienting but no one really knew what to expect. That's the scary part of being a pioneer. I see a dresser with action figures I don't recognize neatly arranged on top. On the floor are a few comic books. I never read comics as a kid. Slowly I manage to lift myself and sit up on the mattress. I put my head in my hands with a splitting migraine. There is a mirror hanging behind the door on the other side of the room. Blood rushes to my head as I stand and I stumble to the mirror. I can only see through pinholes due to the headrush but as I take a few deep breaths my vision clears and I can start to make out the reflection staring back at me, and I suddenly realize..... it's not me. I reach up to touch my face, a strangers face. It is definitely my face, but it's not MY face. Dr. Rockwell never prepared me for this.

"You did a good job," I said to the stuffed duck standing at my cell door. "Yeah, whatever," the duck said. "Not like I got a choice, do I?" I walked outside, hearing the faint sound of music. It was a beat I could work with, but not my favourite. There was a reason bloody goths and death cults liked heavy metal. Korean pop music just didn't quite evoke the right emotions. "Hey, look, this is prison. We ain't got much to work with here." I sighed. "Thanks anyway, Leeroy. Now where are the bodies?" As I walked through the prison, the other inmates stared. You know what they say about the quiet ones? Well, they were all quiet now. "Only the guards?" I asked as I surveyed the bodies. "I thought I told you to get Zeke, too." "He's in solitary. I can only do so much with these." He waved his flappy cotton wings at me. "Now hurry the fuck up and get me out of this body," he snapped. I looked down at my hands. My life is quiet. I live with my husband, who I have been with for 62 years. We've outlived our only child and all of our friends. Our family has all passed, it's just the two of us. We live in the woods, and quiet is the way I like it. I grew up a very quiet person. I never really stood up for myself, and over the years I've realized I live in a nice bubble. As of lately, however, I've become an angry person. I know it's the snoring. Damnit. I can't take it any more. The rising and falling of his chest while he slept used to be beautiful to me. I used to watch, entranced, any time I could not sleep. Now all I can think of is how much I hate the ripping noises his body makes. With each snore, I feel myself growing more impatient. They rip through me, they make me want to rip through him. I used to put a pillow over his face, as a joke, when he would snore. It would wake him up, and we would laugh until we fell back asleep. I did this to him last night. But last week, the silence brought me such relief. So much relief that I couldn't bring myself to lifting the pillow again. Now when I sleep next to my husband, it's very quiet, but I sometimes miss watching his chest rise and fall. FIRST ONE. don't be too harsh:)

It wasn't real. Everyone knew this. Earth had died away a long time ago, its dry arid land unfit for any life worth living. But all the same, it spun on, slowly around the sun. Humanity, tired of a meaningless continuation of destruction and vice, tried something new. Implanting everyone into their own virtual world, a plane of existence that promised happiness and meaning was created. Everyone had their own place and dreams. An ambitious upstart could rise the ranks until he controlled everything, all without disturbing the quiet life of a more peaceful soul. There was no deception. The truth was not concealed. But why would one abandon a life of satisfaction for the reality of death and conflict? Did it matter that it was fake? A love blossomed in VR was no less emotional. The heart did not beat slower because the kiss was not technically given, because the partner did not exist " outside ." The affection was authentic. That was no lie, nothing was hidden. A life of perfection and joy awaited everyone. Their world was destined for them, everything they need and could want was found within. No one had a plan forced upon them unwillingly; everything was fluid and their own. Dreams did not exist, for they became truth. One could affect and influence anything they wanted, whenever they wanted. Nobody doubted this was for the best. The ground was now a green and bountiful paradise, breathing with energy. And like that it would always remain. This is the new reality.

I need to get home. Strangely enough, I felt aches and pains everywhere - but there wasn't a single visible bruise. This line needs to hurry up..... wait, what was I waiting for again? A bored looking young man jotted down notes. Everything was a bit surreal. I knew I was in some sort of enclosed space, but I couldn't see any walls. The floor beneath me felt like it could sink any moment and that notion didn't scare me at all. Bits of conversation faded in and out around me. driving down one of those old roads, cow comes trotting into my lane like some fucking idiot..." "son's okay, but he's going to be upset about it..." It all seemed so natural, but something begged my attention. I didn't remember anything. Finally my turn came, for whatever it was. A bored old man stared up at me, "Name?" I panicked. Name. Goddamn it what is my name? " ..... Let me check the files." A paper appeared out of thin air, "Lydia Andrews. Age 18. Hm..... Interesting. You know how you died?" For some reason, this shocking revelation was old news to me. "No." He sighed and rubbed his temples, but chuckled in a disarming fashion. "Neither do we. Don't worry, it's probably just a filing error. For now we'll send you to Section B13." The crowd went silent and stared at me. If only I knew why it made so self-conscious. "Don't let the reincarnated ones scare you. They've been around the block and love freaking out newcomers. It's temporary, we'll get it fixed in no time." As walked past him..... or through him, I'm not sure. A cat trotted up to me, "Hey - you compulsively honest or something?" I tilted my head, and the creature just repeated himself. "I don't know what you're talking about." Suddenly he jumped in front of me. "He asked you how you died. People spend millennia building up their resume, making it look good, and you could have just said you tried to save a bunch of orphans or something. I wish I could have done that!" Wondering how the cat died, I knelt down and picked him up, placing him on my shoulder. "What did you do?" "I got a little sticker that said:'Roadkill' and was assigned to wander around the car crash dormitory. But hey, I don't envy you - you missed an opportunity like the dumb human you are." Absentmindedly patting the cat on the head, I phased through a couple of walls. "You know what Section B13 is about?" It purred happily, before jumping down to walk beside me. What a strange little cat. "Don't listen to anyone who says it's temporary. Millions of people die everyday, it's not like anyone's going to care about the one person who got assigned wrong. I think I know of like, one girl who got moved. And that was because someone found out that she was serial killer who stole the resume of a doctor." The cat continued, "Anyways, Section B13 is filled with all sorts of people. Mainly those who died from bizarre accidents. It's cold and dark and the electricity is terrible. No one there minds though, they spend most of their time so high that they could relive their deaths and laugh about it."

On the third floor of a condemned building in the Washington Heights neighborhood of Manhattan you put a needle in your arm. Inside the needle's bulb is black liquid, melted tar, heroin, a cheap high, five bucks a gram. You flash the bulb with a drop or two of your blood, it make no difference to the color just the time it takes for the drug to enter your system. You depress the plunger. The ashy elixir disappears into your body. Your perfectly evolved vessel. The one true thing you own. At first you feel hot liquid then it spreads and you feel hot all over. Your heartbeat slows. Time stops. Your eyes droop closed. Life doesn't matter anymore. You float on warm empty clouds and all is nothing. You could ride this forever. And you die. In the condemned apartment building the house-mother says, "fuck that shit." So your friends dump you on the street. A couple riding the wave of gentrification are the first people to not step over your corpse. They call 911. A ambulance arrives. The EMTs aren't allowed to declare you dead so they drive you to the hospital. You are saved by a young doctor from India. He isn't just doing his job. He has a special connection to the soul. He was meant to be a Jain monk. Without knowing what he is doing he accidentally locks your soul in life. You can not die. He has never done this before. He will never do it again. He never knew he did do it until after his own soul left his body sixty years later. He didn't care then though, it was too late to care, death tends to take cares away. He does visit you often and checks your chart and wonders, "how are you alive, but also dead." He studies you. He writes papers about you that no one believes. He violates your privacy for decades. You dont care though. You exist in an unknown blackness. A persistent void. You are moved to the coma ward. Time passes. Your records are lost and recreated over and over again. You age. You are an old man. You become the old man that is just there. You are a withered vessel. You are pitied. There are no questions with answers. Your chest rises and falls. Your heart beats, but you are not dead, but there is nothing that can be done. Switches are pulled, cords are unplugged but you persist. You survive centuries. You survive millenniums. You survive stars in distant parts of the galaxy going supernova. You survive the ort cloud being disrupted by unique gravitational events involving the rotation of the Milky Way which sends streams of icy rocks screaming towards the sun. As those deep space chunks journey your way you continue by surviving hurricanes and earthquakes and volcanic eruptions. You are moved inland when the polar ice plug fails and the oceans rise. Eventually you survive the calamity of the inevitable comet storm and the dust and ash clouds that gather in the atmosphere to eventually rain down. You survive being buried by tons of earth. You survive being forgotten. You survive the wind eating the ground and eventually exposing your useless body. You survive the sun swelling and pushing the planet off its axis causing it to float away from its Goldilock zone. The planet cools just enough to wipe out all life. It is when the last protozoa dies you hear, "Johnny wake up." The request is from a singsongy voice, its the voice of your mother, of God, of potentially everything. You have no choice but to listen to it, so you do, you wake up to the black of your closed eyes. You open your eyes and they part like long healed wounds. Like they weren't ever meant to open. The sound of snapping crusts and scabs is audible. Through cracked and broken eye lids you see the world, not with physical eyes, but with your soul. You part your mouth to scream, but it has also sealed. You tear at the leathery flesh with your knife lengths of brittle nail tipped fingers and peel your lips away, tearing the scab that is your mouth off, exposing the browned and rotten teeth hanging in thick papery gums. Once you free your jaw your mouth flops open useless because your tongue is a flat dried husk. Your throat is just hardened cartilage and sinew. In fact all of your muscles are atrophied jerky over fossilized bones. You know you are because you can think and in thinking, are. But you are the last. You are the last in a brown dead world. You are the last in a brown dead world billions of years away from being eaten by a a slowly expanding red sun. But you are not alone. You have the universe and the universe has you.

Imagine a hammer slamming down on top of your skull, attempting to break through. Imagine every moment it keeps pounding at you trying to leave its mark. The hammering continues to push harder and harder but never breaking skin, much less the bone underneath. I can't think straight anymore. Every moment of concentration is lost by another distraction. Another idea just pops into my head from an unknown source and I am spent with the next hour feeling it reverberate nauseatingly through me until another one willingly takes its place. The thoughts are never my own, and the voices are never ones I recognize. I am a mind reader. It's a rare, but sadly incurable trait that has been passed down through the maternal side of my family for generations. A mother unto a daughter, unto a daughter since ancient times. Some matriarchs in my ancestry were able to use this power to achieve great things. Their wisdom and counsel would allow their partners to achieve great wealth and power. Some generations found their powers revealed to the general public and a hunt for sorcery caused them to be exiled, or otherwise punished for the sinful trait. In the modern generation of things, often I feel I am being punished in a much more passive and cruel way. After all I have to sit here and listen to the ramblings of the old man in the corner, sipping on a cup of coffee and making rude remarks about the high school aged cashier of the local Starbucks. I listen to the pretentiousness of the college student sipping on their Caramel Mocha about the insanity of other students for their lack of understanding semicolons. There is a special place for those who use semicolons in a creative writing assignment; that special place is literally hell. Explaining the plight to my friends has become useless as well. When I explain I couldn't sleep at night because I could hear the whispering mind of a lady walking her dog at 2AM, they believe I was simply dreaming or just hearing things. Many of my friends don't even believe it's a real disorder that I have. I have been asked by others whether or not I have been diagnosed with a form of schizophrenia and just believe in all of this. The rest of my friends have expressed jealousy and wish they could have such a cool ability. It seems great on paper. When I first learned of the family trait it filled me with excitement. I was really looking forward to the day that I would be able to truly understand the depth of another person's mind and thoughts. It seemed exciting, and I imagined that it could help as a career path toward criminal psychology, or at the worst case scenario I would be a damn convincing fortune teller on an east coast boardwalk. Sadly, both for myself and the sake of the stories which I tell my friends, the reality is that a lot of the thoughts I come across aren't as interesting as we like to believe them to be. Most of the things we tend to think about aren't as interesting to another outside perspective. The true problem is a power like this does not simply contain the off switch it needs and sometimes, without realizing it I simply delve into the minds of others almost unknowingly. If it wasn't for the voices being so distinct and unlike mine, half the time I probably wouldn't realize these thoughts are any but my own. I guess to give us the security that there is some sanity to this gift. A common courtesy from the genealogical traits I carry. My coffee cup is empty. I suck the air out of the straw and move it around, hoping that there are a few drops left, but amidst the distractions of everyone else, I became less and less aware of my own time and place. Time to go buy another coffee I suppose. I reach the counter and begin to place my order. Vanilla Soymilk Latte, as per usual. I see the cashier put the order in without even asking me. I've come to this coffee shop for people watching enough times, she clearly remembers it by now. "Will that be all?" Asked the young cashier. I listen to the monotonous clicks of the touch screen. Of course, I thought. She rings up the total and I offer her the money. Suddenly a voice comes ringing through my head. "She seems rather out of it today." Am I that noticeable to others? When you read the minds of others, I suppose it's really hard to save your own face. Half the time I don't even know what I'm thinking. "Stop that!" the same voice shouts. That was the cashier. What is she asking me to stop? Or is it something else? I begin to inspect her mind further. "Get out!" the voice demands. I become more confused. "Hey!" Shouts the cashier. I look at her, a bit shocked and apologize. She realized I was reading her thoughts after all? That doesn't seem likely. Nobody else can read thoughts like I do. I've never seen it before. She hands me the coffee. "Next time, knock on the door. Don't just walk in unannounced. That's bad manners." She remarks casually. "What do you mean?" I ask her cryptically, afraid to listen to her thoughts any futher. She simply says nothing and walks away. I return to my seat, a bit distraught. My mind begins to shut down completely and the voices just begin to roam freely. I can hear many thoughts, but I have become too unfocused to really discern them this time. All I can hear is her voice, shouting back at me "Stop that!" and if anyone else has ever noticed this, but been too shy or uncertain who their mind was speaking to. The voices become more and more silent, and for the first time I can clear my mind almost entirely of them. It's peaceful for a moment and I feel as if I could drift off into a dream state where I don't have to listen to others and can simply find my own mind once again. I follow the silence of it toward my desired salvation. I feel my body fall forward and collapse. "How do you feel?" A voice asks me inquisitively. "Relaxed. Calmed." I reply. "Open your eyes." The voice commands. I blink for a second and raise my head from a couch. I see my friend in a chair beside the couch I am laying on. He is scribbling something down on a piece of paper on the clipboard. "I'm sorry Sophia, but time is up today. Tell me more about the gift next week." My friend tells me. "I can't wait. There is so much more to it." I tell my friend. "I'm sure there is. Are you still involved in the psychology program at the university?" My friend asks. "Of course," I smile. "I want to understand the minds of others in a much better way than this. I want to understand them exactly the way you understand mine."

When the creature looked at the child again she was grinning up at him, holding the suction section of his mouth part between teeth. "Lucy!" I hate it when he calls me that. He steps down from his crystal throne and his posse of angels part before him. The bright white light of eternal paradise spans endlessly in every direction. It's headache inducing. "It's been a while, my friend!" He's all smiles. He knows why I'm here and he's enjoying every second of it. "God, yes it has..." I offer a handshake; he wants to hug. He always wants to hug. "So, I-I was hoping we could talk..... um..... population." I hold his gaze, and his eyes tell me he's not going to make this easy. " Yea, yea - definitely! Hey, can I get you something? A drink? A smoke? Give in to temptation buddy - you know how it is, huh? " He punches my arm lightly and laughter bursts from his lungs. His angelic lackeys giggle among themselves. " I'm good, honestly. I just wanted a quick chat. " " You got it, bro! C'mon, let's go to my office. " He steps forward and places his arm over my shoulder. As much as I hate him, his embrace always makes me feel at home. " Yo G-man! " A deep voice booms behind us. We turn, and a shirtless angel cups his hand around his mouth. " You still on for a jam later? " " You know it, Gabby. " God replies. His words sound deflated, and although he tries to hide it, a grimace flashes across his face. " Wooo! My trumpet's ready for a good hard blowin '! " " Hey ooohh! " He answers, throwing his pinky and ring fingers into the air. " Devil horns... I invented that, you know. " Even I can hear the nerves in my voice. " That's why I love you man. You always were creative. " A floating, luminescent rectangle is the only indication of his so-called office. As we enter, the world around us molds into empty light. " So I wanted to talk to you about... " " Yea, yea - reformation, right? " He cuts me off. " Population. " " Right, right, I gotcha. So what, you guys feeling a little uncomfortable down there? " He laughs at the irony and wrings a long white beard between his fingers. " It's just that there's only so many people we can handle, you know? Dante really, really, oversold our real estate situation. " " I hear ya, but I don't really see how I can help, man. I mean, Hell is Hell, right? " I was expecting some resistance. " Well that's just it. Is Hell really Hell anymore? I mean, two-hundred years back we had a theme. Killers, fraudsters, witches - the clear cut ' bad guy'types. Things made sense. Now... well, there are some that just don't fit. And don't even get me started on the atheist problem. " " No offense, but this sounds like a management issue. You guys should really get in touch with Purgatory about this. " " Have you tried dealing with Purgatory? We've been sending them appeals non-stop for what may as well be eternity. The only things getting sent to limbo are my damn relocation requests. " " Haha, man... you've come a long way. I remember the Lucifer who didn't give a hoot. Now you're all passionate and looking out for people. Where was this guy when I needed him to have my back, huh? " It always stings when he brings up the past, but I know he's just trying to divert the conversation. " Look, your whole brand is based on forgiveness. I'm just asking you to forgive a few hundred million. " " If I start throwing out free absolutions, this whole setup goes to Hell - literally and figuratively. Besides, I love a good confession, man. How do you think the Catholics will react if I start giving everybody prayer-less clean slates? " " They don't have to know about it. " " They'll know, they always know. " " If there's one thing I've learned about deception in my time on this job, it's that if people aren't asking questions, they probably don't want to know the truth. " He sighs and rubs the bridge of his nose for a moment. I see an opening. " Times have changed, man. Back when we first set this up, I'd have people on a fast-track to flames just for wearing the wrong fabric and eating shrimp. Your good book's out of date, and people are too skeptical to accept any modifications. Look what happened to Joseph Smith - did you see that South Park episode? " He stands and cracks his back, exhaling and fluttering his lips. " Can you still beat Randy Rhoads in a guitar duel? " His question catches me off guard. " I don't really see what that has to do with anything? " " I'm just kinda sick of jamming with Gabriel. The guy wants to play all the time and I can't say no... I mean, we go way back. But the guy's an endless source of dick jokes and I need to mix it up. " " I can still play. " " I'll tell you what. You join us for the jam session later, and if you're still half as good as I remember, I'll take as many minor sinners as you can throw my way. The movie pirates and Bush voters - that kind of thing. " I'm taken aback, and try to subdue the grin stretching across my face like wildfire. " It's a deal. You're finally making a pact with the Devil, huh? " I can't resist saying it. " I guess I am. " He smiles.
